Help: the agile kit

Everything here works offline with Git for Windows alone: its Perl and its Vim. The same text is in Vim (:help agile) and on the command line (perl agile.pl help TOPIC, perl agile.pl help search WORDS, perl agile.pl help error "MESSAGE"). Hands-on lessons: perl agile.pl practice.

Generated from vim/doc/agile.txt and vim/doc/agile-errors.txt by perl agile.pl help --html. Edit the source, not this page.

Troubleshooting

Paste the message: perl agile.pl help error "cannot write reports/x.html: Permission denied", or find it below.

  • 1. PROJECT AND FILES
  • no scrum.conf found here or above (run: daily.pl init)
  • cannot write FILE: REASON
  • cannot read FILE: REASON / cannot open FILE: REASON
  • cannot chdir DIR: REASON
  • commands: init new status compile report ...
  • unknown command 'X' (sprint velocity backlog ...)
  • usage: ...
  • 2. COMPILING A STAND-UP FILE
  • FILE: NOT applied
  • FILE:LINE: unknown verb 'X'
  • FILE:LINE: 'VERB' needs a team section (== Team) first
  • FILE:LINE: VERB needs an id (and other missing arguments)
  • FILE: no date (put YYYY-MM-DD in the file name or on the first line)
  • FILE: no sprint number (add 'sprint N')
  • FILE: unknown task 'ID'
  • FILE: task 'ID' already exists
  • FILE: 'ID' is not committed in sprint N for TEAM (at: ACCOUNTS)
  • FILE: 'ID' is not in a backlog or carryover for TEAM (at: ACCOUNTS)
  • FILE: 'ID' has no points to re-estimate
  • FILE: 'ID' is not Done for TEAM in any sprint (at: ...); redo is for finished work
  • FILE is already in JOURNAL: marked it compiled, applied nothing
  • writing JOURNAL failed (...): check the end of the journal ...
  • 3. THE JOURNAL AND LEDGER FILES
  • FILE:LINE: unrecognised line / bad date / bad amount ...
  • FILE:LINE: transaction does not balance (off by N)
  • bad period 'X' (want YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-Qn)
  • evm: budget '~ ...' (FILE:LINE) needs 'from DATE to DATE' ...
  • percent complete for 'ACCOUNT' is not a number / is over 100
  • csv: unknown table 'X' (items sprints epics intake health)
  • 4. THE CHAT, LINT AND ANSWERS
  • ERROR Name: no Y/T/B found / no B found
  • ERROR Name: 'B' appears 2 times: capitalize the one that is the delimiter
  • ERROR Name: T is empty; B is empty (write 'none')
  • ERROR Name: out of order: expected Y ... T ... B ...
  • warn Name: no task id in Y (e.g. B-11) / ID is not in the journal
  • no chat file for DATE / no chat files for DATE / no Y/T/B answers found
  • chat: no team for est lines of tasks not in the journal yet
  • NAME owns tasks in the journal but is not in roster.txt (roster check)
  • 5. MAIL, CALENDAR, AI
  • refusing: fix the marking errors above, or run again with --force
  • warn: marking_owner is empty ... (marking advisories)
  • powershell.exe failed (is this Windows with Outlook installed?)
  • AI request failed: ... / unknown ai_backend / ai_url not set
  • not a git repository (git init first)
  • 6. THE KIT'S OTHER TOOLS
  • FILE: TOOL not found / no converter for .EXT
  • working tree not clean: commit first
  • daily.pl report failed / cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:PORT
  • bad classification 'X'
  • practice: no lesson N / lesson N is not set up
  • release: no profile 'NAME' / a manifest line names a missing file
  • memo-build: FILE: no "## Subject: ..." line / placeholders to fill in
  • pages-index: DIR is not a directory / mkguide: guide.html.in must start with <!DOCTYPE html>
  • 7. IDEF0 MODELS
  • tabs in indentation; use 2 spaces per level
  • cannot parse line / line has no name / no parent
  • outputs declare goes-to with '>', not '<'
  • broken link: cannot resolve 'A|B|Flow'
  • bad suffix / duplicate model letter / more than 9 activities
  • unclosed ```idef0 fence / doc comment / no plate / fmt refusing
  • idef0: idef0_models in sysml.conf is auto, steps or root / ROOT has no steps
  • idef0: skipped: sysml.conf sets no verb_root
  • 8. THE MODEL PORT AND SYSML TOOLS
  • usage: xmi2sysml.pl ... / nothing to do / --req-style is def or usage
  • tools/sysml/sysml.pl not found; structural self-check only
  • FILE:LINE: end tag </X> does not match <Y> (and other XML errors)
  • FILE: IO::Uncompress::Unzip is not available / not a zip / no .reqif file inside
  • FILE: no id column (have: ...); name it with --col id=NAME
  • usage: status-metrics.pl {init,collect,report} ... error: ...
  • json: expected ':' at offset N (metrics.json or history.jsonl)
  • git ...: exit N / gen_cmd ...: exit N / tag ...: not baseline-<number>
  • bad date / bad timestamp / FILE: no date
  • usage: perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl check FILE... / model.pl: no model/ directory
  • new: NAME must be a PascalCase identifier / rename: 'X' already exists
  • idef0: no calc def or action def named 'X' (verb_root in sysml.conf)
  • usage: perl sysml-tree-svg.pl ... / sysml-check: X: no such file or directory
  • FILE:LINE: error: root package 'P' has no @Marking (and the other findings)
  • threat 'T' is not mitigated by any requirement / no CAPEC id
  • sysml-diff: 'git ls-tree ...' failed / REV: no .sysml files under PATH
  • v1v2: FILE: no XMI or ReqIF member found / doors2v2: FILE: empty file
  • --layout-map FILE:LINE: expected PACKAGE = folder/ or PACKAGE = folder/File.sysml
  • FILE: not an xmi2sysml map / not a CHANGES.csv / --impact DIR: not a directory
  • req-recipe: --format is text, csv, junit or codequality / cannot read FILE
  • 9. CODING DRILLS
  • drill: no problem matches 'X'
  • drill: no file FILE (perl drills/drill.pl start ID first)
  • drill: no attempt recorded for ID yet
  • drill: usage: drill.pl COMMAND ...
  • drill: phased: no scenario 'X' / no phase N
  • your file does not load / timeout after 5s / exit(N) called
  • 10. GITLAB, GITFLOW AND THE PIPELINE
  • gitlab.pl: unknown command / --OPTION needs a value / mr new needs --source and --title
  • gitlab.pl: give --url URL or --local DIR / set VAR to a personal or project access token
  • GitLab: METHOD PATH: STATUS MESSAGE / curl exit N
  • GitLab: FILE does not match the registry's sha256
  • GitLab: pipeline must succeed / approvals required / merge conflict
  • GitLab: USER wrote merge request !N and cannot approve it
  • You are not allowed to push code to protected branches on this project.
  • GitLab: no project 'PATH' / no branch or tag 'REF' / no milestone 'NAME'
  • GitLab: tag 'NAME' already exists / another open merge request already exists
  • GitLab: bad time 'X' / unknown access level / an issue needs a title
  • GitLab: bad cron 'LINE': want 5 fields / cron 'LINE' never runs
  • FILE:LINE: label value is '#RRGGBB | description' (the project file)
  • GitFlow: origin has no 'develop' branch (run init first) / not a feature branch
  • GitFlow: drop DIR changes nothing on vendor/prime / merging failed
  • FILE:LINE: job 'NAME': stage 'X' is not in stages / include: local file does not exist
  • gitlab.pl ci: not inside a git work tree / --event tag needs --tag T
  • KIT is not set / the kit on this runner is X, but .kit-version pins Y
  • kickoff: DIR is not empty / --levels is a comma list of names
  • talk: standup needs --as USER / no milestone 'Sprint N'
  • ci-reports: no 'elements=N errors=E warnings=W' line in LOG
  • GitLab: no user given / cannot save STDOUT (a script or the kit itself)
  • 11. INTERNAL INVARIANTS

First day after cloning the kit agile-howto-first-day

You need Git for Windows (Git Bash, its Perl and its Vim). Nothing else.

1. Get the kit. From a clone:

mkdir -p ~/projects && cd ~/projects
git clone URL agile

or from a release zip (agile-release): unzip it, then check it:

sha256sum -c agile-v1.0.zip.sha256

2. Check that it works on this machine (each line ends "all N passed"):

cd ~/projects/agile
for t in tests/*.t; do perl $t | tail -1; done

3. Set up Vim and a shell alias (agile-vimrc, agile-alias):

echo 'syntax on'                               >> ~/.vimrc
echo 'source ~/projects/agile/vim/scrum.vim'   >> ~/.vimrc
echo "alias daily='perl ~/projects/agile/bin/daily.pl'" >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

Tell git who you are once, or daily.pl commit cannot commit:

git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email you@example.com

4. Build the demo project and look at the cockpit (agile-demo):

perl sim/training.pl --fast
perl agile.pl

5. Make your own project (agile-first-project):

daily.pl init ~/scrum/myprogram
cd ~/scrum/myprogram
vim scrum.conf

6. Do practice lesson 1 (agile-practice-1):

perl ~/projects/agile/agile.pl practice 1

You are done when: the tests all pass, vim then :help agile opens this file, perl agile.pl opens the demo cockpit in the browser, and perl agile.pl practice check 1 says "lesson 1: done".

Run the daily townhall agile-howto-townhall

One Teams call for every team, 08:30 to 08:45; people type Y/T/B in the chat. The whole loop is in agile-ytb; the operating model is docs/WORKFLOW.html section 4. Times are a suggestion.

1. 08:05, five minutes of recall (agile-daily-drill):

:SDrill            (or: daily.pl drill)

2. 08:10, draft today's statuses from yesterday's (agile-daily-propose):

daily.pl propose

Paste the block into the meeting chat when it opens.

3. 08:15, cards for each member, optional (agile-daily-cards):

daily.pl cards               (--send mails them through Outlook)

4. 08:30, attendance from the calendar, optional (agile-daily-attend):

daily.pl attend

5. 08:30-08:45, lint the chat while people are still on the call:

:STown                       (\sw)

In Teams: CTRL-A CTRL-C in the meeting chat. In Vim: \sp pastes and lints. \sy puts the replies on the clipboard; CTRL-V them into the chat. :SSend Name opens a 1:1 chat with that person's reply filled in.

6. 08:45, download the meeting's attendance report (Teams: Attendance tab) to standups/DATE-attendance.csv, then:

:SJoined                     (daily.pl joined)

7. After the call, the two minutes at the keyboard:

:SAnswers                    (daily.pl answers --assume)
:STally                      only if there were #est or #vote rounds

Open today's stand-up file (:SNew), uncomment the suggested lines you accept (done, unblock, punt, hold, pass), add anything else, then:

:SDry                        (\sd) shows what compile would write
:SCompile                    (\sc)
:SReport                     (\sr)
daily.pl health
:SDraft                      or daily.pl brief, on mail days
:SCommit

Or all of step 7 after the edits in one go: daily.pl all --draft

You are done when: daily.pl status says "no pending stand-up files", the sprint line shows today's done points, and git log -1 in the project says "standup DATE".

See also: agile-daily-lint, agile-daily-answers, agile-ack, agile-howto-publish.

Plan a sprint (Day 1) agile-howto-planning

1. See what is ready:

daily.pl backlog TEAM        each team's backlog, by priority then age
daily.pl velocity            what each team has been finishing

2. Make today's file and write the plan, one section per team:

:SNew

Under each "== Team" line:

sprint 7
cap 24
commit B-13 Ann Lee
commit B-1221                last sprint's carryover comes back with commit
new! B-16 2 Spike on track fusion p:1 e:"B1 Fire Control" o:"Cy Ray"

The sprint number can be on the second line of the file for all teams.

3. Check the plan before you write it:

:SDry
daily.pl sprint 7            after compile: Load% per team

Load over 100% turns a team amber, over 110% red.

4. Write it and publish:

:SCompile
:SReport
:SCommit

You are done when: daily.pl sprint shows the new sprint with every team's Load% at or under 100%, daily.pl members shows no "unassigned" line, and daily.pl status says "sprint 7: 0/N ... done".

See also: agile-verb-commit, agile-verb-cap, agile-verb-sprint.

Close a sprint: review and report (Day 14) agile-howto-review

1. See what is still open:

daily.pl sprint
daily.pl blocked

2. After the demo, sweep every open task in today's file (:SNew), per team:

done B-11 B-121
carry B-1221                 not finished: to next sprint's planning
drop B-23                    out of the sprint
redo B-101 demo found the reset mail unsent
note retro: pair on the ICD next sprint

3. Compile and write the reports:

:SDry
:SCompile
daily.pl review              the sprint report, reports/sprint-N-report.*
daily.pl report
daily.pl rollup              on the first review of a month

4. Commit and mark the close:

daily.pl commit
git tag sprint-7

You are done when: daily.pl sprint 7 shows Open 0 for every team, reports/sprint-7-report.html exists, and git status in the project is clean.

See also: agile-daily-review, agile-daily-velocity, agile-howto-planning.

Refine the master backlog (Day 9) agile-howto-refinement

1. Intake new work to the master backlog, in today's file:

== Master
new M-2 8 Cross-segment timing budget p:1 e:"E1 Engineer" t:"E Systems"

2. Hand tasks to teams, retire stale ones:

== SEI
refine M-1                   master backlog -> SEI's backlog
prune E-12223 merged into E-12222

3. Size them in the townhall with #est rounds (agile-est-vote), then:

:STally                      writes est lines into today's file

Uncomment the est lines you accept, then :SDry and :SCompile.

You are done when: daily.pl backlog (the master backlog) holds only what you mean to keep, and daily.pl backlog TEAM lists the refined tasks with sizes.

Add a person or a team agile-howto-people

1. A person, name exactly as Teams shows it:

daily.pl roster add "Lee, Ann" ann.lee@example.com Alpha Lead ACME
daily.pl roster              lists and checks against the journal

2. A team appears when a task is filed under it: a "== Gamma" section with a new line, compiled. Give it a capacity with cap at the next planning.

3. Add the new people to the townhall invitation:

daily.pl invite --dry        then without --dry to open it in Outlook

You are done when: daily.pl roster ends ", roster and journal agree".

Write the weekly A-Z metrics report agile-howto-metrics-weekly

The 26 status metrics (A to Z) of a SysML v2 model under the pipeline, collected from the model's git repository and its exports (agile-status-metrics; definitions in docs/STATUS-METRICS.html). To see it work first: perl sim/status-metrics-sim.pl ~/sm-demo builds the 12-week Halberd example (repo, exports, metrics.json, history.jsonl).

1. Once: write metrics.json (repo, exports, segments, totals; Appendix A of docs/STATUS-METRICS.html, or copy the one the simulation writes) and freeze the denominators from the legacy exports:

perl bin/status-metrics.pl init --config metrics.json --xmi legacy.xmi --reqif export.reqif

2. Every working day, after the day's merges (a scheduled task or by hand):

perl bin/status-metrics.pl collect --config metrics.json --history history.jsonl

One snapshot is appended to history.jsonl. --as-of DATE collects a past day.

3. Friday, the report:

perl bin/status-metrics.pl report --config metrics.json --history history.jsonl --out report

It writes report/status-weekly.md (the A-Z table), report/status-daily.csv (open in Excel) and report/dashboard.json.

4. The dashboard: open docs/STATUS-DASHBOARD.html in Edge, paste dashboard.json into the "Data (JSON)" panel and press Apply.

5. For the status memo, paste rows of status-weekly.md into memo.md (agile-howto-memo).

You are done when: report/status-weekly.md has this week's column, the dashboard shows today's date, and history.jsonl has one line per working day.

Port one segment from SysML v1 to v2 agile-howto-port-segment

The legacy model is a Cameo/MagicDraw XMI export; the target is SysML v2 text under model/SEGMENT/ in the model's git repository. The full guide is docs/SYSML-PORT.html; the tools are agile-xmi2sysml, agile-sysml and agile-model-pl. Practice it: agile-practice-8.

1. Export from Cameo: File > Export To > Eclipse UML2 (v5.x) XMI File, with stereotype applications included; save it as exports/DATE-legacy.xmi, outside the model repo.

2. Read the mapping report first (unmapped types, stereotypes not converted, type references not resolved):

perl ~/projects/agile/bin/xmi2sysml.pl --report exports/DATE-legacy.xmi

3. Convert into a branch, grammar-checked:

cd model-repo
git switch -c port/SEGMENT
perl ~/projects/agile/bin/xmi2sysml.pl --out ../scratch --check ../exports/DATE-legacy.xmi
cp -r ../scratch/SEGMENT model/

(Convert into a scratch directory and copy only the segment being ported: a re-run overwrites hand edits. Requirements come out as one-line requirement usages, the form status-metrics counts; --req-style def writes requirement def blocks instead.)

4. Work the TODO lines (each names the v1 type and xmi:id):

:vimgrep /TODO/ model/SEGMENT/**/*.sysml
:copen

5. Check it:

perl ~/projects/agile/tools/sysml/sysml.pl check model/SEGMENT/*.sysml
perl ~/projects/agile/tools/sysml/model.pl lint
perl ~/projects/agile/tools/sysml/model.pl check

In Vim: \mx this file, \ml the model, \mk the outline (agile-vim-sysml).

6. Commit the segment and merge through the gate:

git add -p model/SEGMENT
git commit -m "port: SEGMENT from legacy.xmi DATE"

You are done when: sysml.pl check and model.pl lint exit 0 ("errors=0"), :vimgrep /TODO/ finds none you have not accepted, and the segment is committed.

Import a DOORS export agile-howto-doors

DOORS requirements become SysML v2 requirements carrying their doorsId (agile-reqif2sysml; details in docs/SYSML-PORT.html).

1. Export from DOORS: File > Export > ReqIF (a .reqif or .reqifz) with Object Heading, Object Text, the absolute number and the verification method. CSV is the fallback (columns Object Identifier, Object Level, Object Heading, Object Text, Verification Method).

2. Look first:

perl ~/projects/agile/bin/reqif2sysml.pl --report exports/DATE-system.reqif

3. Convert into the model repo; DOORS drops the module prefix from the absolute number, so put it back with --id-prefix:

perl ~/projects/agile/bin/reqif2sysml.pl --id-prefix SYS- --out model --layout "_reqs/{pkg}.sysml" --check exports/DATE-system.reqif

From CSV: add --csv and --col id="ID" --col text="Requirement" for columns with other names.

4. The trace against the model (metrics C, F, G, I: linked, orphans, unverified, completeness):

perl ~/projects/agile/bin/reqif2sysml.pl --report --model model exports/DATE-system.reqif

5. Commit the requirements files. You are done when: the requirement files pass sysml.pl check, and the --report --model run lists the orphans and unverified ids you will work.

Write a status memo agile-howto-memo

1. Gather the facts (each prints text you can paste):

daily.pl status
daily.pl quad
daily.pl health

2. Write memo.md in Vim: one paragraph per point, lists for sub-points, "# SUBJECT" for a centred heading. Mark portions if your program does: {CUI}phrase{/}. In Vim, :r !daily.pl quad pulls text into the buffer.

3. Render it (agile-memo):

perl ~/projects/agile/tools/memo/md2memo.pl memo.md > memo.pdf
perl ~/projects/agile/tools/memo/md2memo.pl --plain memo.md > memo.txt

From Vim: :!perl ~/projects/agile/tools/memo/md2memo.pl % > memo.pdf

You are done when: memo.pdf opens in Edge with numbered paragraphs (1. a. (1)) and, when marked, the banner on every page.

Publish the reports and the status mail agile-howto-publish

1. Check the marking set-up before anything leaves your desk:

daily.pl check

2. Write every report (reports/ is regenerated each time):

daily.pl report
perl ~/projects/agile/agile.pl ~/scrum/myprogram    the cockpit page

3. Mail (Outlook drafts; nothing is sent until you press Send):

daily.pl draft               the status mail to the leads (to/cc)
daily.pl brief               the short BLUF mail to leadership
daily.pl cards --draft       one card per member (--send sends them)

4. Optionally put today's metrics into the stand-up meeting body:

daily.pl post                (--send also updates the attendees)

You are done when: the drafts are open in Outlook and reports/DATE-status.html matches what you are sending. If a draft is refused, read agile-err-marking-refused.

Track funding and earned value agile-howto-funding

The funding journal is a separate ledger file (not the scrum journal), read by ledger.pl (agile-ledger). The Halberd example has one: run perl sim/halberd-gen.pl, then look at data/halberd/funding.ledger and its complete-DATE.csv files.

1. Write funding.ledger in Vim: book the funds under Assets (so the funding side of a budget is not reported as a budget row), the time-phased budgets, and the spending, e.g. weekly labor:

2026-10-01 Funding received
    Assets:Funding:Halberd      $500,000.00
    Income:Contract
~ Monthly from 2026-10-01 to 2027-01-01
    Expense:Labor:Halberd        $120,000.00
    Assets:Funding:Halberd
2026-10-09 Labor week 1
    Expense:Labor:Halberd         $28,000.00
    Assets:Funding:Halberd

("until" works as well as "to"; a budget is prorated by day at the window edges.) Check it: perl bin/ledger.pl -f funding.ledger check

2. Spending month by month, and against the budget:

perl bin/ledger.pl -f funding.ledger bal -M Expense --depth 3
perl bin/ledger.pl -f funding.ledger budget -M -b 2026-10-01 -e 2027-01-01

3. Earned value: write the percent complete per account in a CSV (complete-DATE.csv, lines "account,pct"), then:

perl bin/ledger.pl -f funding.ledger evm --now 2026-10-31 --complete-file complete-2026-10-31.csv

or give it inline: --complete Expense:Labor:Halberd=40 (repeatable).

4. When does the money run out:

perl bin/ledger.pl -f funding.ledger forecast --now 2026-10-31 --months 2 Assets

5. Put it on the cockpit: in scrum.conf set funding = funding.ledger and complete = complete-*.csv (agile-conf-funding), then perl agile.pl PROJECT and open the Funding tab.

You are done when: ledger.pl check prints "ok", evm shows a CPI and SPI for every account (no "without a percent complete" line), forecast gives a run-out date for the funding account, and the cockpit's Funding tab shows the chart.

See also: agile-ledger-evm, agile-ledger-forecast, agile-ledger-monthly.

Recover from a bad compile agile-howto-bad-compile

A stand-up file with a mistake is rejected whole, every error listed: nothing is half-applied. Fix the lines and compile again.

1. Before compile: :SDry (daily.pl --dry compile) is free. Use it until it prints no errors. Each error names the file and line; look the message up with:

perl ~/projects/agile/agile.pl help error "PASTED MESSAGE"

2. Compiled, but one line was wrong: never edit the journal's history. Post the correction as a verb in a new file: carry what you wrongly marked done, est to the right size, commit what you dropped.

3. Compiled, and the whole file was wrong, not yet committed:

git diff scrum.txt            what the compile appended
git checkout -- scrum.txt

then delete the "# compiled ..." first line of the stand-up file, fix it, and compile again.

4. Compiled and committed:

git revert HEAD

then as in step 3: remove the "# compiled" line, fix, compile.

5. The journal itself will not load (you edited it by hand):

daily.pl status               the first error, with its line number
perl ~/projects/agile/bin/ledger.pl -f scrum.txt check

You are done when: daily.pl status loads without an error and says "no pending stand-up files", and git status is clean after daily.pl commit.

See also: agile-err-not-applied, agile-err-already-compiled.

Back up and commit the project data agile-howto-backup

Each project is its own git repository (daily.pl init made it). The kit's own repository never holds journal data: data/ is ignored.

1. Every day, after compile:

daily.pl commit              git add -A and commit "standup DATE"

2. Once: a second copy on approved storage, a bare repository on a share:

git init --bare //server/share/scrum/myprogram.git
git remote add origin //server/share/scrum/myprogram.git
git push -u origin HEAD

then after each commit: git push

3. Or a single file you can copy anywhere:

git bundle create ../myprogram-DATE.bundle --all

Restore with: git clone myprogram-DATE.bundle myprogram

4. Before a big change (a hand edit of scrum.txt):

git tag before-edit

You are done when: git status is clean, git log -1 shows today, and git push (or the bundle) is up to date. Remember the marking: the repository is marked whenever its content is (agile-conf-banner).

Find help when something is unclear agile-howto-help

1. A command or key:

perl agile.pl help compile          or in Vim: :help agile-daily-compile
daily.pl help lint

2. A word you remember:

perl agile.pl help search carryover

3. An error: copy the message and paste it:

perl agile.pl help error "standups/2026-10-05.txt:7: unknown verb 'don'"

4. The worked example: docs/TRAINING.html replays a whole sprint. You are done when: you found the section; if nothing matched, the words you searched for are worth a note in the help source (vim/doc/agile.txt).

Practise coding for an interview agile-howto-practice-coding

One session (30 to 60 minutes), from Git Bash in the kit, all offline. The full plan for the first 90 days is docs/DRILLS.html; the commands are in agile-drills.

1. Ask what is next:

perl drills/drill.pl next

It names one problem (the first unsolved ladder rung, a failed one to finish, a phased drill, or the weakest section) and why.

2. Read it, ask the eight questions, start the clock:

perl drills/drill.pl start p12-dedup

Your file is ~/drills-work/p12-dedup.pl. Write the assumptions as comments first; say the pattern, the complexity and one edge case aloud.

3. Edit and test, again and again (in Vim: \do opens your file, \dt tests):

vim ~/drills-work/p12-dedup.pl
perl drills/drill.pl test p12-dedup

4. Log it before you stop (minutes and the result are filled in):

perl drills/drill.pl log p12-dedup "hash of seen tokens; forgot //="

5. Only after an honest attempt, compare: perl drills/drill.pl solution p12-dedup.

6. Five minutes of recall in Vim: :DrillTrain (agile-drills-trainer). You are done when: drill.pl test passes, the log has the line, and you could say the pattern and its complexity without the page.

2. GETTING STARTED agile-start

The kit is plain text and core Perl: the journal is a ledger file you edit in Vim, and Perl compiles and reports it. Nothing is installed and nothing needs the network. docs/README.html is the overview, docs/WORKFLOW.html the operating model, docs/TUTORIAL.html the editing walkthrough, and docs/TRAINING.html a replay of one whole sprint.

Getting the kit agile-clone

Clone it anywhere (nothing depends on the location), or unzip a release (agile-release). Git Bash is the shell for everything here. Run the tests

once to know this machine's Perl is fine:

cd ~/projects/agile
for t in tests/*.t; do perl $t | tail -1; done

Layout: bin/ (the commands), lib/ (the modules), vim/ (Vim support and this help), tests/, docs/, sim/ (simulations and generators), tools/ (IDEF0, memo, SysML), data/ (your projects, never committed to the kit).

Setting up Vim agile-vimrc

Add to ~/.vimrc (Git Bash: vim ~/.vimrc):

syntax on
source ~/projects/agile/vim/scrum.vim
let g:markdown_fenced_languages = ['idef0']

The source line adds the :S commands and \s keys (agile-vim), the file types (stand-up, journal, chat, drill, IDEF0) and this help: it registers vim/doc and runs :helptags there when the tags file is missing or older than the help files. The leader key is \ unless you set mapleader. Check with :help agile and :command S.

A shell alias agile-alias

The help writes "daily.pl"; with an alias you can type it that way.

In ~/.bashrc:

alias daily='perl ~/projects/agile/bin/daily.pl'
alias agile='perl ~/projects/agile/agile.pl'

daily.pl finds the project's scrum.conf by searching upward from the current directory, so cd into the project first.

Your first project agile-first-project

One directory per program, its own git repository:

daily.pl init ~/scrum/myprogram
cd ~/scrum/myprogram

init writes scrum.conf, an example scrum.txt (all comments), standups/, reports/, .gitignore and .gitattributes, and runs git init. Then:

1. Edit scrum.conf: recipients, the townhall time, facilitator (your Teams display name), the marking (agile-conf).

2. Add people: daily.pl roster add "Lee, Ann" ann@example.com Alpha Lead ACME

3. Seed the backlog: daily.pl new, then new lines under "== Team" (agile-verb-new), then compile. The first file says "sprint 1"; tasks you commit there start the sprint.

Keep projects anywhere; under the kit, data/NAME is ignored by the kit's git.

Project files agile-files

scrum.conf           settings (agile-conf)
scrum.txt            the journal (agile-journal); compile writes it
standups/DATE.txt    the day's stand-up notes (agile-standup); you write it
standups/DATE[-Team]-chat.txt      the pasted Teams meeting chat
standups/DATE-Team-answers.txt     Y/T/B per person, written by answers
standups/DATE-proposals.txt        written by propose; a +1 accepts a line
standups/DATE[-Team]-attendance.csv  the Teams attendance download
roster.txt           the people: Name | email | Team | Role | Org
attendance.csv       who answered, joined, declined (appended)
drill.txt            your memory-drill progress (personal)
reports/             everything daily.pl report writes; not committed

The demo project (DroneCorp) agile-demo

data/demo is the sample townhall project: DroneCorp, a notional racing-drone company, ten teams, its backlog derived from an IDEF0 model. It is built,

and rebuilt, by the training replay:

perl sim/training.pl --fast
perl agile.pl                 the cockpit for data/demo

training.pl wipes data/demo every run and refuses any other directory (agile-training). A fresh clone has no data/: run it once.

The Halberd project agile-halberd

Halberd is a fictional, notional air and missile defense program used as the running example across the kit. Its pieces:

- data/halberd: the 12-week SysML v1 to v2 port run as a kit project, one team, six sprints, a stand-up every working day, plus funding.ledger and complete-DATE.csv for earned value (agile-howto-funding). Build it:

perl sim/halberd-gen.pl             also writes docs/HALBERD.html
perl sim/halberd-gen.pl --no-html
perl agile.pl data/halberd          the cockpit, with a Funding tab

It reads docs/src/status-metrics.md and checks the compiled journal against it sprint by sprint (agile-halberd-gen).

- docs/HALBERD.html: the same, as a page to read without running anything; docs/STATUS-DASHBOARD.html: the A-Z dashboard with Halberd's numbers.

- examples/halberd: the SysML v2 text model (29 files, seven segments, with SecMeta markings, trust zones and threats) that exercises sysml.pl, model.pl and the views toolkit (agile-sysml-views); its README.md shows every command (agile-model-pl):

perl tools/sysml/model.pl --root examples/halberd lint

- tools/idef0/examples/halberd/halberd.md: the IDEF0 program model, seven models, one per organization (agile-idef0):

perl tools/idef0/idef0.pl lint tools/idef0/examples/halberd/halberd.md

- The status-metrics simulation: perl sim/status-metrics-sim.pl OUTDIR (agile-status-metrics).

Practice lessons 2, 3 and 7 use a copy of data/halberd (agile-practice).

The lab project agile-lab

data/lab is the project for practising the townhall loop without a team: agile-rehearsal writes a realistic chat into it and agile-lab-run runs unattended days against it.

3. DAILY.PL, THE DAY-TO-DAY DRIVER agile-daily

daily.pl [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]       (no command: status)

Every command finds scrum.conf upward from the current directory.

Each day            new  compile  report  draft  brief  commit  all  status
Before the call     drill  propose  cards  attend  invite  meetings
During the call     lint
After the call      answers  chat  joined  ai  post
Views               sprint  velocity  backlog  members  epics  roadmap
                    blocked  quad  health
Reports             review  rollup  csv
Setup and checks    init  check  roster  help

One command's help: daily.pl help COMMAND (or :help agile-daily-COMMAND).

Options for every command agile-daily-options

--today YYYY-MM-DD   act as if it were that day (catch up, replay, rehearse)

-c FILE, --conf FILE use that scrum.conf instead of searching upward

--dry                compile: show what would be written, write nothing;
                     invite: show the invitation, create nothing
--team T             cards, drill: one team
--to A --cc B --subject S   draft, brief: override scrum.conf
--force              draft, brief, cards, invite: go on despite marking errors
--send / --draft     cards: send the mails / open them as drafts; post: send
--reply --confirm --private --table      lint (agile-daily-lint)
--guess --assume     answers (agile-daily-answers)
-n N --sheet --grade FILE                drill (agile-daily-drill)
--until YYYY-MM-DD   invite: the last day of the series

The commands agile-daily-commands

daily.pl help agile-daily-help

daily.pl help COMMAND, daily.pl --help, daily.pl -h Prints this chapter, or one command's section. Works outside a project.

daily.pl init [DIR] agile-daily-init

Make a project in DIR (default: here): scrum.conf, scrum.txt, standups/, reports/, .gitignore, .gitattributes, and git init. Existing files are kept. Prints the next steps. See agile-first-project.

daily.pl new [TEAM...] agile-daily-new

Create (or just name) today's stand-up file standups/DATE.txt: the date, the current sprint, and a "== Team" section per team with its open tasks listed as comments. Prints "created" or "exists" and the path. Vim: :SNew (\sn).

daily.pl status agile-daily-status

The journal at a glance: tasks, current sprint, teams, pending (not yet compiled) stand-up files, and the sprint's done points. The default command. It also proves the journal loads: an error here names the line.

daily.pl compile agile-daily-compile

daily.pl --dry compile Apply every pending stand-up file, oldest first: validate every line, append the ledger entries to the journal, and mark the file "# compiled". A file with any error is NOT applied (every error is listed) and compile stops there. --dry prints what would be appended and writes nothing. Vim: :SCompile (\sc), :SDry (\sd). Errors: agile-err-not-applied.

daily.pl report agile-daily-report

Write every report into reports/: dashboard.html, tree.html, roadmap.html, cockpit.html, DATE-status.html/.txt, DATE-brief.html/.txt, DATE-quad.html/.txt, sprint-N-report.*, MONTH-rollup.*, and the CSVs. Marked when scrum.conf sets a banner. Vim: :SReport (\sr).

daily.pl draft [--to A] [--cc B] [--subject S] [--force] agile-daily-draft

The status mail as an Outlook draft (classic Outlook on Windows): metrics, blockers, today's notes, flags, the AI summary if any. You review and send. Refuses on a marking error unless --force. Vim: :SDraft.

daily.pl brief [--to A] [--cc B] [--subject S] agile-daily-brief

The short leadership mail (one sentence and up to five bullets), as an Outlook draft. Same marking gate as draft.

daily.pl commit agile-daily-commit

git add -A and commit "standup DATE" in the project. Prints "committed" or "nothing to commit". Vim: :SCommit.

daily.pl all [--draft] agile-daily-all

compile, report, (draft with --draft), commit. Stops after compile if a file was rejected. Vim: :SAll (\sa).

daily.pl check agile-daily-check

Load the journal and check the marking set-up: "ok: N tasks, teams ..., sprints ..." and "marking: ok/off" or the problems. Exit 1 on a marking error. Run it after editing scrum.conf.

daily.pl drill [TEAM] [-n 12] agile-daily-drill

daily.pl drill --sheet [TEAM]     daily.pl drill --grade FILE

The memory drill: question cards from the journal and roster (teams and initials, tomes, epics, who owns what, blockers); you type terse answers (ids, codes, initials, any order; ? for don't know, q to stop). Progress is kept in drill.txt (Leitner boxes). --sheet writes reports/DATE-drill.txt to answer in Vim; --grade grades it (what :w does). Vim: :SDrill (\sm).

daily.pl propose [TEAM...] [--private] agile-daily-propose

Today's status for each person, drafted from yesterday's answers and the journal, one paste-ready line each. Writes standups/DATE-proposals.txt so a "+1" in the chat accepts the line (agile-ack). --private writes reports/DATE-propose.html with a 1:1 Teams link per person. Vim: :SPropose.

daily.pl cards [--team T] [--send | --draft] agile-daily-cards

Each member's card (their sprint tasks, blockers, the Y/T/B reminder) to reports/DATE-cards.txt and .html (with Teams 1:1 links). --send mails them through Outlook, --draft opens them as drafts. Vim: :SCards.

daily.pl attend agile-daily-attend

Attendee responses of today's stand-up meetings (Outlook calendar, or the mock fixture) into today's stand-up file as comments and suggested absent lines, and into attendance.csv.

daily.pl invite [--dry] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--force] agile-daily-invite

The recurring weekday townhall in Outlook/Teams, the roster as attendees, at townhall_start for townhall_minutes, the Y/T/B rules in the body. Opens it for you to review and send. --dry prints it only. Refuses an attendee outside mail_domains unless --force.

daily.pl meetings agile-daily-meetings

Today's calendar: time, subject, Teams or not, number invited.

daily.pl lint [FILE | -] [--reply] [--confirm] [--private] [--table] agile-daily-lint

*agile-daily-lint*

Check every Y/T/B status in a pasted chat (default: today's chat files) while people are still on the call. One line per person: FILE:LINE: ERROR|warn|ok Name: reason. "-" reads standard input: powershell Get-Clipboard | daily.pl lint -

--reply      only the lines to paste back into the chat
--confirm    also a read-back for clean statuses (until readback_clean_days)
--private    reports/DATE-lint.html: a Teams 1:1 link per person
--table      what the parser understood: state, who, Y, T, B, note

Exit 1 when any status has an ERROR. Vim: :SLint (\sl), :STown, :SLintReply. The messages: agile-err-lint-no-ytb, agile-err-lint-dup-delim.

daily.pl answers [--guess] [--assume] agile-daily-answers

Parse today's chat files for Y/T/B answers: write standups/DATE-Team-answers.txt, raise flags (silent, blocked N days, same plan N days, unknown ids, done claims), log attendance, and append suggested lines (done, unblock, absent, punt, hold, pass, all commented for you to confirm) to today's stand-up file. --guess accepts the lint's "did you mean" reading where the strict one failed; --assume records the silent with their proposal, marked assumed (never moves points). Vim: :SAnswers.

daily.pl chat [FILE] agile-daily-chat

Tally #est and #vote rounds in today's chat (agile-est-vote) and append est lines (commented unless there was consensus) and vote notes to today's stand-up file. Vim: :STally (\st).

daily.pl joined [FILE...] agile-daily-joined

Teams attendance-report downloads (standups/DATE[-Team]-attendance.csv) into attendance.csv with join, leave and minutes. Vim: :SJoined.

daily.pl ai agile-daily-ai

Build the prompt for your approved AI service from today's answers, flags, metrics and history. With ai_backend = paste it writes reports/DATE-ai-prompt.txt: paste it into the service, save the reply as reports/DATE-ai-response.txt, then daily.pl report includes it. Metrics never come from the AI. Vim: :SAi, :SAiPrompt, :SAiResponse.

daily.pl post [--send] agile-daily-post

Today's metrics text into each stand-up meeting's body in Outlook; --send also sends the update to the attendees.

daily.pl roster agile-daily-roster

daily.pl roster add "Name" email Team "Role" "Org" List the people by team and check them against the journal (owners not in the roster, team mismatches, missing e-mail). add adds or updates a person; the name must be exactly what Teams shows.

daily.pl health [TEAM] agile-daily-health

Every metric of the operating model against its threshold: blocked age, load, done by day 8, velocity, predictability, carryover, bus factor, unassigned, on-time, punt rate, backlog depth and age, intake, epic targets, consensus, declines, silence. One line per signal with what to do. Exit 1 on a red.

daily.pl review [N] agile-daily-review

The sprint report (Day 14) for sprint N (default: current): per team commit, done, carry, load, velocity, predictability, punts, interrupts; printed and written to reports/sprint-N-report.txt and .html.

daily.pl rollup [YYYY-MM] agile-daily-rollup

The monthly roll-up (epics, intake vs done, backlog age, attendance), printed and written to reports/MONTH-rollup.txt and .html.

daily.pl csv [TABLE] agile-daily-csv

TABLE is items, sprints, epics, intake or health: one table to the screen. No TABLE: all of them to reports/TABLE.csv (UTF-8 with a BOM, for Excel).

daily.pl quad [TEAM] agile-daily-quad

The weekly quad: Technical Priorities (TODO, OPEN, DONE, WAIT, HOLD, PUNT, DROP with REDO, PASS, SYNC marks), Watch Items, 30/60/90 Milestones, Accomplishments, and the punt-rate table. Vim: :SQuad.

daily.pl sprint [N] agile-daily-sprint

Per team: capacity, committed, done, open, carryover, removed, done %, load %; then each team's open tasks. Vim: :SSprint.

daily.pl velocity agile-daily-velocity

Committed and done per sprint per team, and the average done.

daily.pl backlog [TEAM] agile-daily-backlog

The master backlog, or one team's: id, points, priority, epic, owner, age, title. Vim: :SBacklog.

daily.pl members [TEAM] agile-daily-members

Each owner's work in progress, done this sprint and queued, and committed tasks with no owner. Vim: :SMembers.

daily.pl epics agile-daily-epics

Roll-up by tome and epic: tasks, points, done, in sprint, backlog, done %.

daily.pl roadmap agile-daily-roadmap

Epics by tome across sprints, with a forecast from velocity. Vim: :SRoadmap.

daily.pl blocked agile-daily-blocked

Blocked tasks, oldest first, with days blocked: over 3 "escalate", over 5 "yours". Vim: :SBlocked.

4. THE STAND-UP FILE AND ITS VERBS agile-standup agile-verbs

standups/DATE.txt is where you type. One verb per line under a "== Team" header; ; or # starts a comment. A file with any error is rejected whole.

More files on one day are fine: DATE-b.txt. Example:

2026-10-05
sprint 7
== Alpha
done A-11 A-12
block A-13 waiting on the ICD from SEI
new A-14 5 Login MFA p:1 e:"A1 Access" t:"A Platform" o:"Lee, Ann"
note Bob out Friday
Verb                   Does                                  Points move
done ID...             finished (passed the Definition of Done)
                                                   Committed -> Done
carry ID...            not finished; to next sprint  Committed -> Carryover
drop ID...             out of the sprint             Committed -> Removed
commit ID [OWNER]      into this sprint     backlog/carryover -> Committed
new ID PTS TITLE [p:N e:EPIC t:TOME o:OWNER]   intake  -> Backlog:Team
new! ID PTS TITLE ...  intake straight into this sprint    -> Committed
refine ID              master (or another team's) backlog -> this team's
prune ID REASON        retire a backlog task           Backlog -> Removed
est ID PTS             re-estimate (posts the difference)
assign ID OWNER        change the owner
block ID REASON        blocked (WAIT on the quad) until unblock ID
hold ID REASON         interrupted (HOLD) until resume ID
punt ID REASON         too hard as written          Committed -> Backlog
redo ID REASON         found wrong after the demo     Done -> Committed
pass ID TEAM           another team should do it   -> TEAM's Committed
sync ID ID...          coordinated across teams; they share DONE
cap N                  the team's capacity this sprint
note TEXT  risk TEXT  absent NAME...                  report only
sprint N               the sprint (top of the file, or in a section)

The rules of the file agile-standup-rules

- The date comes from the file name (standups/2026-10-05.txt) or a YYYY-MM-DD line at the top.

- "== Team" starts a team's section; "== Master" is the master backlog (new lines there go to Backlog:Master); "==" alone ends a section.

- Quote values with spaces: o:"Bob Ray", e:"B1 Fire Control". commit and assign take the rest of the line as the owner: commit A-1 Bob Ray.

- Owner names must be spelled exactly as Teams shows them; "Last, First" works everywhere.

- Ids are any word without spaces (A-11, HAL-3). Several ids on one done, carry, drop, unblock or resume line are fine.

- A first line "# compiled DATE" means the file was applied; compile skips it. Never remove that line unless you have taken its entries out of the journal (agile-howto-bad-compile).

- In Vim, CTRL-X CTRL-K completes a task id from the journal.

The verbs one by one agile-verb-list

done ID... agile-verb-done

Committed -> Done in this sprint, for each id. The task must be committed in this sprint for this team (agile-err-not-committed).

carry ID... agile-verb-carry

Committed -> Carryover: not finished. The next sprint's planning brings it back with commit ID.

drop ID... agile-verb-drop

Committed -> Removed: out of the sprint and out of scope. For a task still in a backlog use prune.

commit ID [OWNER] agile-verb-commit

Into this sprint's commitment, from the team's backlog, the master backlog or last sprint's carryover; the owner is optional (the rest of the line).

new ID PTS TITLE [p:N] [e:EPIC] [t:TOME] [o:OWNER] agile-verb-new agile-verb-new!

new! ID PTS TITLE ...                                       *agile-verb-new!*

Intake: a new task into the team's backlog (or, under "== Master", the master backlog). new! puts it straight into this sprint and tags it interrupt: 1, so interrupts are measurable. p: priority (lower first), e: epic, t: tome, o: owner. The id must be new (agile-err-task-exists).

refine ID agile-verb-refine

From the master backlog (or another team's backlog) into this team's.

prune ID REASON agile-verb-prune

Retire a backlog task: to this sprint's Removed; the reason is kept on the posting. For committed work use drop.

est ID PTS agile-verb-est

Re-estimate to PTS wherever the task's points are: the difference is posted, history stays. #est rounds in the chat write these lines (agile-est-vote).

assign ID OWNER agile-verb-assign

Change the owner (the rest of the line).

block ID REASON agile-verb-block agile-verb-unblock

unblock ID                                               *agile-verb-unblock*

Mark a task blocked, with the reason; it shows in every report, aging, until unblocked. Over 3 days: escalate; over 5: yours (agile-daily-blocked).

hold ID REASON agile-verb-hold agile-verb-resume

resume ID                                                 *agile-verb-resume*

Interrupted by higher-priority work: stays committed, HOLD on the quad.

punt ID REASON agile-verb-punt

Too hard as written (any reason): Committed -> the team's backlog (TODO) for replanning. Counted in the punt rate.

redo ID REASON agile-verb-redo

Found wrong after the demo: last sprint's Done -> this sprint's Committed.

pass ID TEAM agile-verb-pass

Started it, another team should do it: the whole task to TEAM's Committed in the same sprint; that team assigns an owner.

sync ID ID... agile-verb-sync

Tasks coordinated across teams this sprint: they share DONE (none counts until all are done).

cap N agile-verb-cap

The team's capacity this sprint (load = committed / cap).

note TEXT agile-verb-note agile-verb-risk agile-verb-absent

risk TEXT                                                   *agile-verb-risk*
absent NAME...                                            *agile-verb-absent*

Report-only lines: they appear in the status mail and reports, move no points. "note retro: ..." records a retro action.

sprint N agile-verb-sprint

The sprint the file (or the section) belongs to. Without it, the journal's current sprint. The first file of a project says sprint 1.

5. THE JOURNAL (SCRUM.TXT) agile-journal

A double-entry ledger in ledger-cli format. A task's points move between

accounts, and the account they sit in is the task's state:

Backlog:Master -> Backlog:TEAM -> Sprint:N:TEAM:Committed -> Done
                                                -> Carryover
                                                -> Removed

Equity:Intake balances new tasks. Points are conserved; history is never

rewritten. Compile writes almost everything; you read it (:SJournal, \sj).

An entry is a date, a payee, and postings that sum to zero:

2026-09-23 Intake B-11 Define Software Requirements
    Backlog:BMC2       5 SP   ; id: B-11, epic: B1 Fire Control, owner: Ann, prio: 1
    Equity:Intake

A capacity block:

~ Sprint 7
    Alpha    24 SP

Task metadata agile-journal-meta

On a posting comment, "key: value" pairs after "; ". Later values override earlier ones.

id        the task id (required on every posting that moves a task)
title     from the payee after the id, or title:
prio      priority, lower first
epic      the epic ("B1 Fire Control"); tome  the tome above it
owner     the owner (Teams display name)
team      the team
blocked   the blocker reason; empty = unblocked
hold      the hold reason; empty = resumed
punt redo pass sync    set by those verbs

interrupt 1 on new! tasks

target    YYYY-MM-DD: the epic's target date (on any of its tasks)

Editing the journal by hand agile-journal-edit

Only three safe cases, none of which move points: metadata fixes (owner, epic, tome, prio on an intake line; :%s works for a renamed tome), bulk intake at program start (better: sim/idef0-backlog.pl, agile-idef0-backlog), and capacity blocks. After any hand edit: daily.pl status (it re-reads the journal and reports the first error with a line number), then commit. Never renumber or delete postings: corrections are new postings.

6. SCRUM.CONF agile-conf

key = value lines; # starts a comment; paths are relative to the file. daily.pl init writes a commented one. daily.pl check validates it.

The keys agile-conf-keys

journal agile-conf-journal

The journal file. Default scrum.txt.

standups agile-conf-standups

The stand-up directory. Default standups.

reports agile-conf-reports

Where report writes. Default reports (keep it out of git).

unit agile-conf-unit

The unit of the points: SP by default (Halberd uses items).

to agile-conf-to agile-conf-cc

cc                                                             *agile-conf-cc*

Recipients of draft and brief (comma-separated).

subject_prefix agile-conf-subject_prefix

Put at the start of every mail subject, e.g. INTERNAL.

banner agile-conf-banner

The marking banner (INTERNAL, COMPANY CONFIDENTIAL, ...). Empty: nothing is marked. When set, every report, mail and printed page carries it, and the marking gate runs before mail (agile-err-marking-refused).

marking_owner agile-conf-marking_owner agile-conf-marking_category agile-conf-marking_handling agile-conf-marking_poc

marking_category                                 *agile-conf-marking_category*
marking_handling                                 *agile-conf-marking_handling*
marking_poc                                           *agile-conf-marking_poc*

The marking block under the banner: who owns the material, its category, handling, and who to ask. check warns when owner or POC is empty.

mail_domains agile-conf-mail_domains

Comma-separated domains; mail may only go to them (check, draft, brief, cards, invite refuse otherwise).

history_days agile-conf-history_days

Previous days of answers used for "stuck" and "blocked N days". Default 5.

default_team agile-conf-default_team

The team of standups/DATE-chat.txt when the file name has no team.

facilitator agile-conf-facilitator

Your Teams display name (; between several): your own chat lines are not linted as statuses.

readback_clean_days agile-conf-readback_clean_days

After this many clean statuses in a row a person gets a read-back only on errors (lint --confirm). Default 5.

townhall_subject agile-conf-townhall_subject agile-conf-townhall_start agile-conf-townhall_minutes agile-conf-townhall_location

townhall_start                                     *agile-conf-townhall_start*
townhall_minutes                                 *agile-conf-townhall_minutes*
townhall_location                               *agile-conf-townhall_location*

The invitation daily.pl invite creates: subject, start (HH:MM), length in minutes, location (default "Microsoft Teams Meeting").

calendar agile-conf-calendar

outlook (default) or mock.

calendar_fixture agile-conf-calendar_fixture

With calendar = mock: a JSON file of events (examples/cal-fixture.json; make one from the real calendar with cal.pl dump). Everything then runs offline.

standup_match agile-conf-standup_match

A pattern that picks the stand-up meetings out of the calendar. Default stand-?up.

team_from_subject agile-conf-team_from_subject

A pattern whose first group is the team in a meeting subject.

attendance agile-conf-attendance

The attendance log. Default attendance.csv.

min_minutes agile-conf-min_minutes

joined: fewer minutes than this counts as brief. Default 3.

drill agile-conf-drill

The memory-drill progress file. Default drill.txt.

funding agile-conf-funding agile-conf-complete

complete                                                 *agile-conf-complete*

funding = FILE: a ledger journal of the program's money; the cockpit then has a Funding tab (funds remaining, burn per month, run-out date, a chart, earned value). complete = GLOB: the percent-complete CSVs; the newest one dated on or before today feeds earned value. Both relative to the project directory. See agile-howto-funding.

ai_backend agile-conf-ai_backend

paste (default: write the prompt, you paste the reply), curl (an OpenAI-style endpoint through Git's curl) or mock (tests).

ai_url agile-conf-ai_url agile-conf-ai_model agile-conf-ai_key_env agile-conf-ai_curl agile-conf-ai_curl_args agile-conf-ai_mock_response

ai_model                                                 *agile-conf-ai_model*
ai_key_env                                             *agile-conf-ai_key_env*
ai_curl                                                   *agile-conf-ai_curl*
ai_curl_args                                         *agile-conf-ai_curl_args*
ai_mock_response                                 *agile-conf-ai_mock_response*

For ai_backend = curl: the endpoint, the model name, the NAME of the environment variable that holds the key (never the key itself), the curl command (default curl) and extra arguments. ai_mock_response is the canned reply for mock.

7. THE CHAT: Y/T/B STATUSES, #EST AND #VOTE agile-ytb

People post one line in the meeting chat, capital Y T B as separators, task

ids in it:

Y did B-11   T doing B-12   B none

Also accepted: "Y: ... / T: ... / B: ..." on separate lines, yesterday:

today: blockers:, and 1/2/3. A name before the Y is ignored. Lowercase y t b work only when unambiguous. A person's last message wins, so a repost replaces the first.

What lint checks: the three fields are there, in order, not empty; Y and T each name a task id; the ids exist in the journal. ERROR means the status cannot be used; warn means it parses but says little.

The replies (lint --reply) go back into the chat, or 1:1 with --private: "Did you mean: ...?" for an error, "Got it. Add the task id next time" for a warning, and with --confirm a read-back "I read your status as: ...".

Acknowledging a proposed status agile-ack

After daily.pl propose, a person accepts their proposed line by typing +1, y, ok or a thumbs-up. answers and lint read standups/DATE-proposals.txt.

#est and #vote rounds agile-est-vote

In the meeting type "#est B-104"; people answer with numbers. "#vote Ship Friday? y/n" or "#vote Name: A B C" for a vote. After the meeting paste the chat (:SChat) and run :STally (daily.pl chat): each round is tallied (consensus, or median with outliers; plurality, majority or tie) and written into today's stand-up file as est lines (ready when there was consensus, commented otherwise) and note vote lines. Without markers: chat.pl --est ID --since 09:07 FILE (agile-chat-pl).

An answer is a number with an optional unit ("5", "8 pts", "2 days"), optionally after "actually", "make it", "I'd say" and the like, or before "maybe"; "?" or "idk" for unknown. Anything else is discussion: it never replaces a vote, so "that is not 3 days" is not a vote of 3. Someone who wrote in a round but gave no answer is listed as "could not read". Lines for tasks not yet in the journal (and vote notes) go under default_team in scrum.conf, or under the team named in the file (standups/DATE-Team-chat.txt).

8. AGILE.PL: THE COCKPIT, HELP AND PRACTICE agile-pl

agile.pl [--no-open] [--today D] [PROJECT] agile-cockpit

Rebuild PROJECT's reports (daily.pl report) and write ./dashboard.html next to agile.pl, the cockpit: one self-contained page with daily, weekly, sprint, monthly, backlog tree, roadmap, quad, people and IDEF0 tabs, and open it. PROJECT defaults to data/demo. --no-open only writes the file. --today sets the cockpit's date. Vim: :SCockpit.

agile.pl serve [--port 8090] [PROJECT] agile-serve

The same page served on http://127.0.0.1:8090/, rebuilt on every load, with a "Rebuild reports" button. Localhost only. CTRL-C stops it.

agile.pl help [TOPIC | search WORDS | error MSG] agile-help-cmd

This help on the command line. TOPIC is a tag (agile-daily-lint), a command (lint, compile), a verb (carry), a scrum.conf key (banner), a Vim command (STown) or a runbook (townhall). Also:

--html [FILE]   regenerate docs/HELP.html from vim/doc/
--md [FILE]     regenerate docs/help/quickref.md (the binder chapter)
--check         what the help is missing: untagged commands, keys, verbs,
                conf keys; messages not in the catalog; broken links
--tags          every tag

agile.pl practice [N | check N | reset N] agile-practice-cmd

The lessons (agile-practice): no argument lists them; N sets up lesson N in data/practice/lessonN and prints the task; check N says what is done and what is missing; reset N removes the sandbox. --dir DIR puts the sandboxes elsewhere.
