10. SCRUM.PL, LEDGER.PL, CAL.PL, CHAT.PL agile-lowlevel

Lower-level tools over one layer each, for scripting and ad hoc questions. They do not read scrum.conf, so their output is never marked: use daily.pl for anything that leaves your desk.

scrum.pl agile-scrum

perl bin/scrum.pl [-f JOURNAL] [--today D] COMMAND [N] [ARGS]

-f FILE (or $SCRUM_FILE; default scrum.txt), --today, --last N (velocity), -o FILE (dashboard, roadmap, tree, csv), --to --cc --subject (draft), --text (email). N is a sprint number (default: current). help: perl bin/scrum.pl help [COMMAND].

sprint [N] agile-scrum-sprint

The sprint table and open tasks.

velocity [--last N] agile-scrum-velocity

Committed and done per sprint; average over the last N finished sprints.

backlog [TEAM] agile-scrum-backlog

The master backlog or a team's.

members [TEAM] agile-scrum-members

Per owner: in progress, done, queued.

epics agile-scrum-epics

Roll-up by tome and epic.

roadmap [-o FILE] agile-scrum-roadmap

Epics by tome across sprints as text, or an HTML page with -o.

items [STATE] [TEAM] agile-scrum-items

Raw task query; STATE is master, backlog, committed, done, carryover, removed or closed: scrum.pl items committed Bravo.

dashboard [-o FILE] agile-scrum-dashboard

A self-contained HTML dashboard (default dashboard.html).

tree [-o FILE] agile-scrum-tree

The backlog tree as HTML (default tree.html).

email [N] [--text] agile-scrum-email

The status mail, HTML (or text) on the screen.

draft [N] --to A [--cc B] [--subject S] agile-scrum-draft

That mail as an Outlook draft.

csv [TABLE] [-o FILE] agile-scrum-csv

items, sprints, epics, intake or health as CSV.

check agile-scrum-check

Load the journal: "ok: N items, teams ..., sprints ...".

ledger.pl agile-ledger

perl bin/ledger.pl [-f FILE] [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ACCOUNT-REGEX...]

A plain-text double-entry ledger (ledger-cli format), used for the scrum journal and for anything else: money, hours, funding. -f FILE (or $LEDGER_FILE; default ledger.txt). Account regexes after the command are ORed, case-insensitive: bal groceries repairs.

-p PERIOD (2026, 2026-09, 2026-Q3)  -b DATE (from)  -e DATE (before)
--depth N  -C cleared only  -R real only  -E show zeros  --payee RE
-M, --monthly  month by month (bal, reg, budget)
--now YYYY-MM-DD   the status date of evm and forecast (through the end of
                   that day; default today)
--months N     forecast's burn window (default 3)
--complete ACCOUNT=PCT  --complete-file FILE   evm's percent complete

help: perl bin/ledger.pl help [COMMAND].

bal [ACCOUNT...] agile-ledger-bal agile-ledger-balance

The balance tree. ledger.pl -f scrum.txt bal Sprint:42 shows a sprint.

reg [ACCOUNT...] agile-ledger-reg agile-ledger-register

One line per posting with a running balance.

budget [-p PERIOD] agile-ledger-budget

The ~ periodic budget entries against the actuals (default: this month).

-M, --monthly agile-ledger-monthly

With bal: an account by month table with a Total. With reg: one line per account per month with a running total. With budget: Month, Account, Budget, Actual, Remaining for each month.

evm [--complete ACCT=PCT]... [--complete-file F] [--now D] agile-ledger-evm

Earned value per account: Account, %done, BAC, BCWS (planned), BCWP (earned = BAC x percent complete), ACWP (actual), CV, SV, CPI, SPI, EAC, VAC, and a Total. Needs dated budgets: "~ Monthly from YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD" (or "until"). Percent complete: --complete ACCOUNT=PCT, repeatable, PCT as 0-100, 0.x or 55%; or --complete-file FILE, CSV lines "account,pct" (a header and # comments are allowed). An account's percent covers its sub-accounts. --now sets the status date (default today).

forecast [--months 3] [--now D] [ACCOUNT...] agile-ledger-forecast

Funding run-out per account: Account, Balance, Burn/month (the average monthly spend over the last N whole months), Months left, Runs out. forecast --months 2 Assets limits it to the funding accounts.

csv agile-ledger-csv

Postings as CSV: date,status,payee,account,amount,commodity.

check agile-ledger-check

Parse and verify every transaction balances: "ok: N transactions".

accounts agile-ledger-accounts agile-ledger-payees

payees                                                   *agile-ledger-payees*

The distinct account or payee names.

cal.pl agile-cal

perl bin/cal.pl [--mock FIXTURE.json] [--date D] COMMAND

The Outlook calendar through PowerShell COM (classic Outlook only). list (default), dump (JSON; save it as a fixture for calendar = mock), attend [MATCH], lines [MATCH], post ID|MATCH [--file F | --text T] [--send], create --subject S --start DATETIME [--attendee A]... [--weekdays], ps (print the PowerShell it would run).

chat.pl agile-chat-pl

perl bin/chat.pl [--est ID | --vote Q] [--since HH:MM] [--lines] FILE|-

Tally #est and #vote rounds in a pasted chat; --est/--vote tally without markers from --since; --lines prints the stand-up lines; --messages lists the parsed messages.

11. IDEF0 MODELS agile-idef0

An IDEF0 model is plain text: a model line, activities nested by two spaces, ports with links. tools/idef0/idef0.pl validates and renders it; the cockpit's IDEF0 tab shows the plates. The full reference is

tools/idef0/README.md.

# -*- mode: idef0 -*-
tD Design                         t model, letter D
  a# Define Quad Spec             a activity
    i# Pilot Requirements         i input, c control, m mechanism
    o# Quad Spec > F|Cut Frame Parts|Quad Spec    o output, > goes to

# or ; starts a comment, ## a doc comment. A model is a .idef0 file, a

.txt file whose first line is the mode line, or ```idef0 blocks in Markdown.

idef0.pl COMMANDS agile-idef0-commands

perl tools/idef0/idef0.pl COMMAND FILE...

idef0.pl lint FILE... agile-idef0-lint

Validate; FILE:LINE: error|warning: ...; exit 1 on errors. Lint every model of a project in one command so links between models resolve.

idef0.pl text FILE... agile-idef0-text

The plates as character art, form-feed paginated.

idef0.pl html FILE... agile-idef0-html

A drawing set in one HTML page, the plates as SVG.

idef0.pl svg NODE FILE... agile-idef0-svg

One plate (e.g. E22) as a standalone SVG.

idef0.pl dump FILE... agile-idef0-dump

The numbered model tree(s).

idef0.pl links FILE... agile-idef0-links

The project's interface table.

idef0.pl fmt [--number|--auto] [--write] FILE... agile-idef0-fmt

Rewrite tag suffixes: --number freezes the derived numbers, --auto puts # back (models keep their letter); --write edits in place. fmt checks structure only, not links.

The wrappers idef0lint, idef2text, idef2html, idef2svg, idef0fmt do the same. Keep rendered output out of the model directory: a *.txt glob would lint a plates.txt as a model.

IDEF0 in Vim agile-vim-idef0

In an IDEF0 buffer (and Markdown with ```idef0 blocks):

\il  :IdefLint          lint this file; errors to the quickfix list
\iL  :IdefLintProject   lint every model in this directory
\iv  :IdefPlates        the plates as text in a split
\id  :IdefDump          the numbered tree
\ik  :IdefLinks         the interface table
\in  :IdefNumber        fmt --number on this file
\iu  :IdefAuto          fmt --auto on this file
\if  :IdefFollow        jump to the target of this line's < or > link
\io                     a new sibling line below, in insert mode
za zc zo                fold a subtree (folds follow the indentation)

:IdefLint :IdefLint \il

\il                                                                      *\il*

Save and lint this file; the errors open in the quickfix list (:cn next).

:IdefLintProject :IdefLintProject \iL

\iL                                                                      *\iL*

Lint every *.txt and *.idef0 in this file's directory together, so links between models resolve.

:IdefPlates :IdefPlates \iv

\iv                                                                      *\iv*

The project's plates as text in a scratch split.

:IdefDump :IdefDump \id

\id                                                                      *\id*

The numbered node tree.

:IdefLinks :IdefLinks \ik

\ik                                                                      *\ik*

The interface table.

:IdefNumber :IdefNumber \in

\in                                                                      *\in*

fmt --number --write: freeze the derived numbers into the tags.

:IdefAuto :IdefAuto \iu

\iu                                                                      *\iu*

fmt --auto --write: back to # (models keep their letter).

:IdefFollow :IdefFollow \if

\if                                                                      *\if*

Jump to the port at the other end of this line's link.

\io \io

A new line below with the same indent and tag letter, ready to type a name.

From a model to a backlog agile-idef0-backlog

perl sim/idef0-backlog.pl MODEL.md [--date D] [--sprint N] [--cap N --commit]
perl sim/idef0-backlog.pl MODEL.md --roster [--people N]

Turns a model into a planning stand-up file the kit compiles: model -> tome and team, level-1 activity -> epic, leaf -> task, cross-model link -> an interface task in the destination team. --cap N --commit also commits each team's top tasks up to N. This is how data/demo is built.

12. WRITING: MEMOS AND DOCUMENTS agile-writing

md2memo.pl agile-memo

perl tools/memo/md2memo.pl [--ps|--text|--plain] [--font times|courier]
     [--indent PTS] [--mark] [--default CLS] [--banner page|doc] FILE.md

Markdown to a DoD-style memorandum on US Letter, 1" margins: numbered paragraphs (1. a. (1) (a)), uppercase headings, ruled tables, code blocks. Output: PDF (default), PostScript (--ps), text with underline (--text) or plain ASCII (--plain), to standard output. Pure Perl; no TeX or Office. Marking: tag a phrase {CUI}...{/} or {S//NF}...{/}; each portion is marked in the margin with the roll-up of its tags, and every page gets top and bottom banners. The full syntax is at the top of tools/memo/md2memo.pl; a worked example is tools/memo/examples/status-report.md. Runbook: agile-howto-memo.

docs2txt.pl agile-docs2txt

perl bin/docs2txt.pl FILE...                text of each file
perl bin/docs2txt.pl -o DIR FILE...         DIR/NAME.txt per file
perl bin/docs2txt.pl grep [-i] PATTERN FILE...   FILE:LINE: match
perl bin/docs2txt.pl tools                  which converters were found

Read PDF, .docx, .doc, .odt and .html as text through converters Git for Windows ships (pdftotext, docx2txt, antiword, odt2txt). Vim: :SDocs. :r !perl ~/projects/agile/bin/docs2txt.pl grep -i shall spec.pdf pulls the "shall" statements into the buffer, to turn into new lines.

13. THE KIT ITSELF: TESTS, RELEASE, PIPELINE agile-kit

Tests agile-tests

for t in tests/*.t; do perl $t | tail -1; done   every suite, one line each
perl tests/help.t                                one suite, every check

Each suite ends "# all N passed". Run them after pulling a new version and before you change anything in bin/ or lib/.

release.pl agile-release

perl bin/release.pl [--tag v1.0]

A zip of the committed tree (no data/, no reports) in release/agile-TAG.zip with a SHA-256 beside it, for another machine. Refuses on uncommitted changes. On the target: sha256sum -c the .sha256, unzip, then daily.pl init in a project directory.

perl bin/release.pl --profile mbse [--tag v1.0]
perl bin/release.pl --profile mbse --list [--worktree]

A slimmer zip, release/agile-NAME-TAG.zip, holding only the files the profile's manifest tools/gitlab/NAME-release.txt lists (one path or glob per line; a line starting with ? is optional). The mbse profile is what an MBSE DevSecOps team needs: the tools, the Vim setup, the GitLab templates and samples, the Tidewater drops, the guides and the primer. --list prints the files instead of packing them (--worktree: from the working tree, not the last commit).

devsecops.pl agile-devsecops

perl bin/devsecops.pl [--quick] [--open]

Runs the kit's own pipeline gates here (the tests under every Perl found, syntax checks, a secrets scan, the marking gate, repository hygiene) and writes ./devsecops.html, a status dashboard. --quick skips the test suites. Exit 1 on a gap.

townhall.tcl agile-townhall-tcl

wish ~/projects/agile/bin/townhall.tcl ~/scrum/myprogram

The meeting console (Tcl/Tk as shipped with Git for Windows): a paste box that saves and lints the chat on every paste, the replies with a copy button, the roster ticking off who answered, and buttons that run the daily.pl commands. It draws only; daily.pl decides everything. :STown is the keyboard-only twin.

14. SIMULATIONS, TRAINING AND PRACTICE PROJECTS agile-sim

Standalone tools in sim/, outside the tested kit. Each one's options are at the top of the file.

sim/training.pl [--fast] agile-training

Wipes and rebuilds data/demo by really running one sprint of daily.pl and git commands (planning, ten townhall days, refinement, review), narrated, and writes docs/TRAINING.html, a playable replay. --fast skips the pauses. Refuses any directory not named demo unless --force.

sim/halberd-gen.pl [--dir PATH] [--no-html] agile-halberd-gen

Builds data/halberd (agile-halberd) from docs/src/status-metrics.md: 56 stand-up files compiled through the real pipeline, checked sprint by sprint against the document. --dir must end in data/halberd (it is wiped). Writes docs/HALBERD.html unless --no-html.

sim/rehearsal.pl [--date D] [--seed N] [--mistakes N] [--silent N] [--out F] agile-rehearsal

*agile-rehearsal*

Writes a realistic Teams chat paste into the current project's standups/: one status per task owner, in the styles people use, with the usual mistakes seeded and N people silent. The answer key goes to the error output: who is wrong and why. Then practise lint, answers and the replies.

sim/lab-run.pl [--days 10] [--start D] [--seed N] [--fix 0.7] agile-lab-run

N unattended townhall days against the current project: rehearsal, lint, replies, reposts, answers, confirming the suggested lines, compile, report, commit; anything unexpected is written to the report as a finding.

sim/history-gen.pl [--dir PATH] [--sprints N] [--seed N] agile-history-gen

Two years of ten teams (data/history) compiled through the real pipeline, and HISTORY.html: every sprint coloured by the status leadership would have seen.

sim/drill-sim.pl, sim/fuzz-chat.pl, sim/daily-job-sim.pl agile-sim-other

Stress tests of the memory drill and the chat parsers, and a time-accounting simulation of the role at scale (docs/SCHEDULE.html).

15. MODEL-BASED TOOLS (SYSML, STATUS METRICS) agile-mbse

These tools are separate from the scrum journal.

status-metrics.pl agile-status-metrics

perl bin/status-metrics.pl init    --config metrics.json --xmi legacy.xmi --reqif export.reqif
perl bin/status-metrics.pl collect --config metrics.json [--as-of DATE] --history history.jsonl
perl bin/status-metrics.pl report  --config metrics.json --history history.jsonl --out DIR
perl bin/status-metrics.pl COMMAND --help

The 26 status metrics (A to Z) of docs/STATUS-METRICS.html, from a SysML v2 model repository and its exports (separate from the scrum journal). init freezes the denominators from the legacy XMI and ReqIF once; collect appends one snapshot a day to the history; report writes status-weekly.md, status-daily.csv and dashboard.json (paste it into docs/STATUS-DASHBOARD.html, "Data (JSON)", Apply). Needs git on PATH. metrics.json names the repo, the exports directory, the segments and totals, and lint_cmd / gen_cmd (the commands it runs: tools/sysml/model.pl lint prints the elements=N errors=E warnings=W line it reads). The repo conventions it expects (model/SEGMENT/, doorsId on requirements, CODEOWNERS, baseline-N tags, exports gate.log, ci_jobs.csv, tracker/sprint-N.csv ...) are in "Running it in this kit" at the end of docs/STATUS-METRICS.html. perl sim/status-metrics-sim.pl OUTDIR builds the 12-week Halberd example (repo, exports, metrics.json, history.jsonl). Runbook: agile-howto-metrics-weekly.

xmi2sysml.pl agile-xmi2sysml

perl bin/xmi2sysml.pl --report FILE.xmi
perl bin/xmi2sysml.pl --out DIR [--layout '{seg}/{pkg}.sysml'] [--check] FILE.xmi
perl bin/xmi2sysml.pl --stdout FILE.xmi

A SysML v1 XMI export (Cameo / MagicDraw) to SysML v2 text, one file per top-level package (DIR/SEGMENT/PACKAGE.sysml). --report: elements in by xmi:type, ported vs remaining (metric A), stereotypes, the unmapped list. Nothing is dropped: what has no mapping becomes a // TODO line with its xmi:id. Options: --req-style usage|def (usage, the default: one-line requirement usages, the form status-metrics counts; def: requirement def blocks), --name PKG (the package for elements outside any package), --check (also run tools/sysml/sysml.pl check over the output). Exit 0 ok, 1 when the self-check or --check finds a problem, 2 on bad usage or unreadable input. The output is deterministic, and a re-run overwrites hand edits: convert into a scratch directory once a segment is hand-fixed. Runbook: agile-howto-port-segment.

perl bin/xmi2sysml.pl --out DIR --layout-map layout.map [--map MAP.csv] FILE.xmi
perl bin/xmi2sysml.pl --delta OLD.xmi NEW.xmi
perl bin/xmi2sysml.pl --delta OLD.xmi NEW.xmi --impact MODEL_DIR [--map OLD-MAP.csv] [--impact-csv F]

--layout-map FILE puts each top-level package at a fixed path (lines "Stations = physical/stations/" or "Types = library/Types.sysml", # comments, "* = unsorted/" for the rest); use one map for every drop, so the paths stay the same and vendor-branch merges stay three-way. --map FILE writes a CSV from every v1 element (xmi:id) to its v2 name, file and line. --delta compares two drops of the same model by xmi:id: added, removed and changed elements, each marked carried (re-convert and merge) or manual (the converter leaves it as a TODO: rework by hand), ending with a manual-rework checklist. --impact MODEL_DIR adds, per change, what it touches in the government's v2 model: requirements satisfied, verification cases, connections, allocations, references to a renamed element, and hand edits to redo. With the prime's CHANGES.csv beside NEW.xmi, the report is grouped by change request.

reqif2sysml.pl agile-reqif2sysml

perl bin/reqif2sysml.pl --report [--model DIR] FILE.reqif
perl bin/reqif2sysml.pl --out DIR [--layout '{seg}/{pkg}.sysml'] [--check] FILE.reqif|.reqifz|.csv

DOORS requirements (ReqIF, zipped ReqIF, or a CSV export) to SysML v2 requirements with their doorsId, one file per DOORS module. --report counts requirements, verification methods, headings, orphans and links; with --model DIR it adds the trace against existing SysML v2 text (C linked, F orphans, G unverified, I completeness). Options: --req-style usage|def (usage is the default), --id-prefix SYS- (put the module prefix back on absolute numbers), --id-attr / --vm-attr / --text-attr / --heading-attr NAME (ReqIF attribute names), --attr NAME (copy an attribute, repeatable), --name PKG, --csv with --col id=NAME --col text=NAME --col heading=NAME --col level=NAME --col vm=NAME, --sep C, --stdout, --check. A heading without text becomes a nested package; text becomes a requirement; neither becomes a TODO. --layout-map FILE maps DOORS module names to paths, as for xmi2sysml. The --model trace also reports drift: a requirement whose doc text in the model differs from the DOORS text (markup and whitespace ignored), listed with both versions. Runbook: agile-howto-doors.

sysml.pl agile-sysml

perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl check FILE...     file:line:col: error: ...; exit 1
perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl corpus [DIR...]   every .sysml/.kerml under DIRs
perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl tokens FILE       the token stream (debugging)
perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl grammar           rules, keywords, symbols
perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl crosscheck [N] [SEED]   against the Pilot (needs Java)

A SysML v2 / KerML syntax checker generated at start-up from the official grammars vendored in tools/sysml/vendor. A diagnostic names the furthest token the grammar could not accept and what it expected there. corpus with no directory checks the 404 vendored library and example files (about 40 s). Details: tools/sysml/README.md. In Vim: \mx (agile-vim-sysml).

model.pl agile-model-pl

perl tools/sysml/model.pl [--root DIR] COMMAND [options]

The project tool for a SysML v2 text model: the project is the nearest directory upward holding model/ (or --root DIR), configured by its sysml.conf (noun_root, verb_root, ...). Commands:

lint [--no-grammar]   SysML checks without Java; prints "lint: N file(s), E
                      error(s), W warning(s)" and "elements=N errors=E
                      warnings=W" (status-metrics' lint_cmd); exit 1 on errors
check                 the 2..9 outline rule and the @L level tags; exit 1
stats                 size, counts, nesting, depths, then check
nouns | verbs [--plain] [--ascii]   the part tree / the function tree
docs                  regenerate docs/Nouns.md, Verbs.md, idef0/, Traceability.md
idef0                 regenerate docs/idef0/ only (through tools/idef0)
trace [--strict]      requirement -> satisfied by -> verified by
tags                  a Vim tags file: CTRL-] on a name or a DOORS id
new part NAME --in PARENT | new verb NAME --in PARENT   scaffolding
rename OLD NEW [--write] [--any]    rename a definition everywhere (dry run)
backlog [--agile=DIR]  the IDEF0 set as a planning stand-up file (sim/idef0-backlog.pl)
precommit | install-hooks   the pre-commit checks / install the git hook
validate              full compile with the Pilot engine (needs Java; exit 3
                      without it)
libnames DIR          refresh the offline standard-library names
draw tree|trace|ibd|pkg [-o FILE]   an SVG view (agile-model-draw)
plates [-o DIR]       drawing plates from the views (agile-model-plates)
diff OLD_DIR | diff --git REV   a change, as pictures (agile-model-diff)
threats [--today D]   the threat table and its checks (agile-model-threats)
gate [--today D]      the validate gate, PASS or FAIL (agile-model-gate)

The worked example is examples/halberd (its README shows every command): perl tools/sysml/model.pl --root examples/halberd lint. In Vim: agile-vim-sysml.

sysml.conf keys agile-sysml-conf

key = value lines, # comments, in the project's top directory:

title          used in generated document titles
noun_root      the part def at the top of the part tree
verb_root      the action (or calc) def at the top of the function tree
level_tags     the @L metadata names, level 1 first (L1Network, L2Segment, ...)
idef0_name     docs/idef0/NAME.md; model_letter: the IDEF0 letter of the root
idef0_models   auto | steps | root: one IDEF0 model per step (steps), one
               model whose boxes are the steps (root, for steps without
               sub-steps), or root when every step is a leaf (auto, default)
steps          name:LETTER:Label, ... (only with idef0_models = steps)
control_types  item types drawn as IDEF0 controls; alloc_prefix: the feature
               path that stands for the verb root in allocate statements
layers         package layers, lowest first; the pipeline's complexity job
               fails an import from a higher layer
acronyms, need_prefix   word splitting; the id prefix of stakeholder needs

model.pl draw pkg draws packages, dependencies and cycles without markings when no package carries @Marking (sysml-pkg-svg.pl --no-markings); model.pl gate still requires them.

The SysML views toolkit agile-sysml-views

tools/sysml/views/ holds standalone core-Perl tools that read any SysML v2 text model (a directory or files) and draw or check it. Each one runs on its own (perl tools/sysml/views/TOOL.pl ...); model.pl draw, plates, diff, threats and gate run them on the current project's model/ and pass every other option through (a --root after the command is the tool's, not the project's). Diagnostics are GNU format, FILE:LINE: error|warning|note: ...; exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 usage or input error. Outputs are deterministic: pin dates with --today / --date. The security checks read the SecMeta library (tools/sysml/views/library/ SecMeta.sysml; copy it into model/): @Marking { level = Level::U; } on every root package, @TrustZone { zone = Zone::dmz; } on parts at a boundary, @SecurityRequirement and @Mitigates { threat = "t"; } on requirements, and threats as metadata t : Threat { stride; capec; asset; mitigation; } lines (or @Threat on an element). DrawingMeta.sysml beside it adds @Drawing for plates. The binder scripts sysml-gate.pl and sysml-trace.pl (text checks, satisfied + verified leaves) are in views/binder/. Golden harness: bash tools/sysml/views/tests/run.sh (tests/sysml-views.t runs it). Usage of every tool: tools/sysml/views/README.txt. A live view beside Vim: agile-sysml-view.

model.pl draw agile-model-draw agile-sysml-tree-svg agile-sysml-trace-svg agile-sysml-ibd-svg agile-sysml-pkg-svg

                                                    *agile-sysml-tree-svg*
                                                   *agile-sysml-trace-svg*
                                                     *agile-sysml-ibd-svg*
                                                     *agile-sysml-pkg-svg*
perl tools/sysml/model.pl draw tree|trace|ibd|pkg [-o FILE] [options]
perl tools/sysml/views/sysml-tree-svg.pl [-o tree.svg] DIR|FILE...

One SVG view of the model, written to KIND.svg in the current directory (or -o FILE), titled "TITLE: ..." from sysml.conf unless --title is given.

tree   sysml-tree-svg.pl: the part decomposition, left to right, each part
       expanded through its type (--root NAME, --all, --depth N, --features,
       --outline, --hide-meta A,B, --compare OLD [--changed]).
trace  sysml-trace-svg.pl: satisfying parts | requirements with S/V status
       | verification cases; the same leaf and gap counts as the binder's
       trace (--gaps, --match REGEX, --package P, --mono for print,
       --compare OLD [--changed]).
ibd    sysml-ibd-svg.pl: parts, ports and connections colored by trust zone;
       error: a zone crossing no satisfied @SecurityRequirement covers
       (by its subject, or named in the connection's secReq attribute);
       warning: fromZone/toZone attributes that disagree with the zones;
       note: the attack surface (--root NAME).
pkg    sysml-pkg-svg.pl: packages, dependencies and markings; errors: a
       root package with no @Marking, write-down (a lower package imports or
       references a higher one); warnings: text leakage, dependency cycles
       (--nested, --hide P,Q, --levels U,CUI).

Open the SVG in a browser: hover for links, tooltips carry doc and FILE:LINE. Halberd's four views: docs/img/halberd-*.svg (perl sim/halberd-views.pl). In Vim: \mw \mq \mi \mp (:SysDraw).

model.pl plates agile-model-plates agile-sysml-plates

                                                      *agile-sysml-plates*
perl tools/sysml/model.pl plates [-o DIR] [--date D] [--source T] ...

Drawing plates (ISO 5457 sheet, ISO 7200 title block) from the model's view usages, or one per top tree, wired def, trace and packages with --auto or when the model has no views. Writes DIR/NUMBER.svg and DIR/plates.html (default DIR: plates; print it to PDF from the browser). Options: --size auto|A4..A0, --color, --owner, --creator, --approver, --status, --rev, --date (default today), --prefix DWG, --source (default git describe), --min-text MM. @Drawing { ... } (DrawingMeta.sysml) overrides any field.

model.pl diff agile-model-diff agile-sysml-diff

                                                        *agile-sysml-diff*
perl tools/sysml/model.pl diff [-o PREFIX] [--changed] OLD_DIR [NEW_DIR]
perl tools/sysml/model.pl diff [-o PREFIX] --git OLD[..NEW] [PATH...]

A model change as a review: PREFIX-tree.svg and PREFIX-trace.svg colored by change (added green, changed amber, removed red), PREFIX-packages.svg and PREFIX-ibd.svg of the new version, and PREFIX-changes.txt (GNU format, for the merge request or Vim's quickfix). The markings, zones and threats checks run on both sides: "new finding" / "resolved". The new side defaults to this model (NEW_DIR, or the working tree's model/ with --git). Exit 1 when the change adds a requirement gap or an error finding. --today D is passed to the threat check. --git needs git (Git Bash).

model.pl threats agile-model-threats agile-sysml-threats

                                                     *agile-sysml-threats*
perl tools/sysml/model.pl threats [--today YYYY-MM-DD]

The threat table (threat, STRIDE, CAPEC, mitigated by, status), then the checks: every threat has one of the six STRIDE categories and a CAPEC-n id (SEC-2); every threat is named by a @Mitigates on a requirement that is satisfied and verified (SEC-3); a current @RiskAcceptance (approver set, expires >= today) turns an open threat into a listed warning; a threat's mitigation attribute must match its @Mitigates. Exit 1 on errors.

model.pl gate agile-model-gate agile-sysml-check

                                                       *agile-sysml-check*
perl tools/sysml/model.pl gate [--today D] [--strict] [--only a,b]
                               [--svg DIR]

The validate gate in one command (sysml-check.pl): text (bare imports, keywords as names, units, docs, braces), trace (every leaf satisfied and verified), markings, zones, threats; one line at the end: check: N check(s) run, E error(s), W warning(s) -> PASS|FAIL. Exit 0 pass, 1 fail. Accepted risks are listed but pass unless --strict. --svg DIR also writes the four pictures. On Halberd it fails on exactly the planted gaps: 7 trace, 1 zone crossing, 2 threats. In Vim: \mg (:SysGate), findings in the quickfix list.

The live viewer: sysml-view.tcl agile-sysml-view agile-sysml-svg2tk

                                                      *agile-sysml-svg2tk*
wish bin/sysml-view.tcl [PROJECT-DIR] [--view tree|trace|ibd|pkg] [--root NAME]
wish bin/sysml-view.tcl PROJECT-DIR --view V --export-ps FILE
perl tools/sysml/views/svg2tk.pl FILE.svg

A window beside Vim (Tcl/Tk as shipped with Git for Windows: wish.exe) that shows one view of the model and redraws within a second or two of a save. The drawing comes from the same drawers as agile-model-draw; Tk cannot show SVG, so svg2tk.pl turns each SVG into canvas primitives (size, rect, line, poly, text, title lines). Keys: 1-4 the view, + - zoom, 0 fit, r redraw, q quit; the wheel zooms, a right-drag pans. Hover shows the element; a click copies its FILE:LINE and writes it to ~/.sysml-view/jump (Vim's \mo opens it). Vim's \mf writes the name under the cursor to ~/.sysml-view/focus: the viewer highlights it and scrolls to it ("follow" re-roots the IBD there). --export-ps draws once, writes PostScript and exits (printing, tests; headless: xvfb-run -a wish ...). PROJECT-DIR defaults to the nearest directory upward holding model/. In Vim: \mW.

v1v2.pl, doors2v2.pl: the fallback converters agile-v1v2 agile-doors2v2

                                                          *agile-doors2v2*
perl tools/sysml/v1v2.pl inventory|check MODEL   (.xmi, .uml or .mdzip)
perl tools/sysml/v1v2.pl convert MODEL -o DIR [--package 'A::B']
perl tools/sysml/v1v2.pl reqs REQS -o F.sysml --package NAME
perl tools/sysml/doors2v2.pl -o DIR [--tests MODULE] EXPORT...

The main path is agile-xmi2sysml and agile-reqif2sysml (they write the forms the status metrics count). Use these when that path cannot read the export: v1v2.pl takes older Cameo exports and the .mdzip project file itself (inventory, a pre-conversion check, convert one package slice with stubs, a --typemap for unresolved types; writes ids.tsv and CONVERSION.txt); doors2v2.pl takes DOORS 9 / DOORS Next CSV or TSV in UTF-8, UTF-16 or Windows-1252 and ReqIF, keeps headings, information objects (as comments), links (verify, satisfy, derive, refine, trace) and the DOORS ID. Both are deterministic: re-run after each export and review with model.pl diff. Details: docs/SYSML-PORT.html, "Fallback converters".

SysML in Vim agile-vim-sysml

In a .sysml buffer (vim/ftplugin/sysml.vim; :make uses vim/compiler/sysml.vim), inside a project with model/ above it. Results go to the quickfix list.

16. PRACTICE LESSONS agile-practice

Hands-on lessons in sandbox projects under data/practice/ (ignored by git; throw them away any time). Each lesson sets up a fresh project, prints the

task, and checks your result:

perl agile.pl practice                list the lessons
perl agile.pl practice 1              set up lesson 1, print the task
perl agile.pl practice check 1        what is done, what is missing
perl agile.pl practice reset 1        remove the sandbox

Work inside the sandbox (cd data/practice/lesson1). The task text below

says daily.pl for perl KIT/bin/daily.pl (agile-alias). Each check prints "lesson N: done" when everything is right.

Lesson 1: the first stand-up file and compile agile-practice-1

Sandbox: a new, empty project (daily.pl init). Task:

1. Make today's file: daily.pl new (or :SNew in Vim).

2. Under its "sprint 1" line add a team and three tasks, and commit two of them with a capacity:

== Alpha
cap 10
new AL-1 3 Set up the build p:1 e:"A1 Tooling" o:"Ann Lee"
new AL-2 5 Write the ICD p:2 e:"A1 Tooling" o:"Bob Ray"
new AL-3 2 Draft the test plan p:3 e:"A1 Tooling" o:"Ann Lee"
commit AL-1 Ann Lee
commit AL-2 Bob Ray

3. daily.pl --dry compile until it is clean, then daily.pl compile.

4. daily.pl status, daily.pl sprint, then daily.pl commit. Check: three or more tasks in the journal, two or more committed in sprint 1, a capacity for sprint 1, no pending stand-up file, and a git commit.

Lesson 2: carry, block and unblock agile-practice-2

Sandbox: a copy of the Halberd project, mid-sprint, compiled up to yesterday. Task:

1. daily.pl sprint: note the open tasks of the current sprint.

2. In today's file (daily.pl new), block the oldest open task with a reason: block HAL-N waiting on the shared runner. Compile.

3. Make a second file for today, standups/DATE-b.txt, with the same first two lines (the date, sprint N) and "== Halberd". In it: unblock that task, and carry another open task. Compile.

4. daily.pl blocked (now empty), daily.pl commit. Check: today a task was blocked with a reason and unblocked again, a task went to Carryover today, nothing pending, and a commit after the set-up.

Lesson 3: close the sprint and report agile-practice-3

Sandbox: a copy of the Halberd project, mid-sprint. Task: close the current sprint as on Day 14 (agile-howto-review).

1. daily.pl sprint: every open task.

2. In today's file mark each one done or carry, compile.

3. daily.pl review, daily.pl report, daily.pl commit. Check: no open points left in the current sprint, reports/sprint-N-report.txt and reports/DATE-status.html exist, nothing pending, a commit after the set-up.

Lesson 4: the townhall chat lint agile-practice-4

Sandbox: the DroneCorp backlog planned yesterday, with today's chat pasted in standups/DATE-chat.txt by sim/rehearsal.pl (mistakes seeded). The answer key is in .answer-key.txt; read it after you try. Task:

1. daily.pl lint: who has an ERROR and why (agile-ytb)?

2. daily.pl lint --reply: the replies you would post.

3. For each ERROR, add a corrected repost at the end of the chat file, as the person would post it: a line "[9:01 AM] Name" then their status "Y ... T ... B none" with their task ids. Their last message wins.

4. daily.pl lint again until there is no ERROR, then daily.pl answers. Check: lint finds no ERROR in today's chat, and today's answers file exists. In Vim the same is :STown, \sp, \sl.

Lesson 5: the memory drill agile-practice-5

Sandbox: the DroneCorp project. Task:

1. daily.pl drill --sheet Contracting (or :SDrill Contracting in Vim).

2. Open the sheet it names; answer at least six cards after the ">" marks: ids, codes, initials. Look things up with daily.pl backlog Contracting and daily.pl members Contracting first if you like: that is reading, the drill is recall.

3. Grade it: daily.pl drill --grade reports/DATE-drill.txt (or :w). Check: drill.txt holds at least six graded cards and at least one right.

Lesson 6: IDEF0 lint, fix, plates agile-practice-6

Sandbox: model/, a five-model IDEF0 project with errors seeded in model/design.txt. Task:

1. perl KIT/tools/idef0/idef0.pl lint model/*.txt (or \iL in Vim).

2. Fix every error (agile-err-idef0-tabs, agile-err-idef0-direction and the others in agile-errors) until lint says 0 error(s).

3. The plates:

perl KIT/tools/idef0/idef0.pl html model/*.txt > plates.html
perl KIT/tools/idef0/idef0.pl text model/*.txt > plates.txt

Check: lint reports no errors, and plates.html holds SVG plates newer than every model file.

Lesson 7: a status memo agile-practice-7

Sandbox: the Halberd project and memo.md, a memo with TODO marks. Task (agile-howto-memo):

1. daily.pl status and daily.pl quad for the facts.

2. Replace every TODO in memo.md; say which sprint this is ("sprint N").

3. perl KIT/tools/memo/md2memo.pl memo.md > memo.pdf perl KIT/tools/memo/md2memo.pl --plain memo.md > memo.txt

Check: no TODO left, the current sprint number named, memo.pdf is a PDF newer than memo.md, and memo.txt exists.

Lesson 8: port a segment to SysML v2 agile-practice-8

Sandbox: legacy.xmi (a small Cameo export, tests/fixtures/xmi2sysml) and an empty model repository (git init) with a sysml.conf. Task (agile-howto-port-segment):

1. perl KIT/bin/xmi2sysml.pl --report legacy.xmi: how many elements are left as TODO?

2. perl KIT/bin/xmi2sysml.pl --out model --check legacy.xmi

3. perl KIT/tools/sysml/sysml.pl check model/*/*.sysml (or \mx in Vim).

4. Work the TODO lines: :vimgrep #// TODO# model/**/*.sysml. For each one either model the element by hand or keep the line and mark it reviewed by changing "// TODO" to "// TODO(reviewed)". Write in NOTES.txt one line, "TODO: N", N being the number of TODO lines left (count lines, not the report's figure: :vimgrep shows them).

5. git add model NOTES.txt, git commit -m "port: legacy.xmi". Check: .sysml files under model/, sysml.pl check passes, every TODO line is fixed or marked TODO(reviewed), NOTES.txt says how many are left (and the number is right), and the work is committed.

Lesson 9: a coding drill, start to log agile-practice-9

Sandbox: an empty drills workspace (the sandbox directory itself; give it to drill.pl with --dir, as the lesson prints). Task (agile-howto-practice-coding):

1. perl KIT/drills/drill.pl show p12-dedup --dir SANDBOX: read it twice.

2. perl KIT/drills/drill.pl start p12-dedup --dir SANDBOX

3. Write the solution in SANDBOX/p12-dedup.pl (vim; a hash of seen tokens).

4. perl KIT/drills/drill.pl test p12-dedup --dir SANDBOX until it passes.

5. perl KIT/drills/drill.pl log p12-dedup --dir SANDBOX "what was slow" Check: p12-dedup was started, the file is no longer the stub, a passing test is recorded, and the drill log has p12-dedup as passed.

Lesson 10: your first model change agile-practice-10

Lessons 10-13 follow Tidewater, a fictional coastal weather network: the prime contractor keeps its SysML v1 model in Cameo and delivers it as drops; the government team (Jim, Bob, Tom) keeps a SysML v2 text copy. Sandbox: the model repository a team gets in week zero, made by tools/gitlab/kickoff.pl scaffold, with drop v1.0 converted into it by the layout map .ci/layout.map (each package at a fixed path, in every drop). model/library/conventions/Conventions.sysml holds the government's level tags; .ci/outline-max records the outline findings drop v1.0 brought with it. You are Bob, the MBSE engineer. About 30 minutes. Task:

1. Look around (a configuration item's folders and its history):

ls model model/physical
git log --oneline

2. Count the TODO lines the converter left: the port's open action items.

grep -rc "// TODO" model

3. vim model/physical/stations/Stations.sysml, then /StationSegment and n until the cursor is on "part def StationSegment {". The next line is a TODO: in v1 a profile stereotype said StationSegment is level 2.

4. Replace that whole line (cc deletes it and starts typing, Esc ends):

@L2Segment;

The tag is the v2 form of the stereotype: metadata defined once in model/library/conventions/Conventions.sysml, one line in place of a profile.

5. Under the line "package Stations {" open a line (o) and type the import that makes the tags visible here, then :w

private import Conventions::*;

6. Check it as a reviewer would, without leaving Vim: \mx the grammar of this file, \ml lint for the whole model (0 errors, 0 warnings), \mk the outline and level tags ("@L tag mismatches 0"; the 20 outline findings are the ones drop v1.0 brought). :copen lists findings; Enter on one jumps to its line. Lint does not catch a misspelled tag (@L2Segmnt;); practice check 10 does.

7. Record the change with its reason (a configuration change, signed):

git add model
git commit -m "Tag StationSegment with its level (L2Segment)"

Check: StationSegment carries @L2Segment; and no TODO, package Stations imports Conventions, the grammar check and lint pass, every level tag sits at its level, and the change is committed.

Lesson 11: your first merge request agile-practice-11

Sandbox: an offline GitLab (SANDBOX/gitlab) holding the Tidewater model project: kickoff.pl scaffold on main, develop from it, the scaffold's .gitlab/project.conf applied, and drop v1.0 merged into develop through vendor/prime (merge request !1). Issue #1 asks Bob for lesson 10's change. Your clone is SANDBOX/work; env.sh makes gl mean perl KIT/bin/gitlab.pl. You are Bob. About 40 minutes. Task:

1. Once in each Git Bash window:

cd SANDBOX/work
source ../env.sh
gl issue list
gl issue show 1

The issue is the action item: no change without one.

2. A branch for this change, from develop (a working copy of the baseline for one change request):

gl flow start feature 1-tag-stationsegment

3. Make lesson 10's change in model/physical/stations/Stations.sysml, but type the tag WITHOUT its semicolon, on purpose: @L2Segment Add the import line as in lesson 10. Then:

git add model
git commit -m "Tag StationSegment with its level (L2Segment)"

4. Push and open the merge request: the change request goes to review.

gl flow finish --title "Tag StationSegment with its level" --description "Closes #1"

The pipeline runs at once and fails: the automatic part of the review.

5. Read why:

gl mr show 2
gl pipeline show N

(N is the pipeline number mr show prints.) Open the grammar job's log at the path it prints: "Stations.sysml:14:9: error: unexpected 'doc'". Try gl mr merge 2: GitLab refuses, "pipeline must succeed".

6. Fix it on the same branch: add the ";" in Vim, then

git commit -am "Add the missing semicolon"
gl flow publish
gl mr show 2

The new pipeline passes. A push updates the same merge request. The test count still shows failures: the outline findings drop v1.0 brought, within what .ci/outline-max allows, so the job passes.

7. Approval, the CCB signature: gl mr merge 2 is refused again, "approvals required". Jim approves; then you merge:

gl --as jim mr approve 2
gl mr merge 2
gl issue show 1

Issue #1 closed itself: the merge request said "Closes #1".

8. Back to the shared baseline:

git checkout develop
gl flow sync

Check: a merge request from your feature branch to develop that says Closes #1, one red pipeline seen and a green one last, approved by someone else, merged; issue #1 closed; develop's Stations.sysml has the tag and the import.

Lesson 12: a prime drop agile-practice-12

Sandbox: lesson 11's project, later: Bob's tag is merged; DR-5 asked the prime for a humidity sensor, and Bob modeled an interim HumiditySensor on develop meanwhile; issue #3 asks Tom to take in drop v1.1, just delivered to SANDBOX/drops/v1.1. You are Tom, who keeps the vendor branch. About 45 minutes. Task:

1. cd SANDBOX/work, source ../env.sh, then gl issue show 3: the intake checklist, a receiving inspection for a contract delivery.

2. What changed, in the prime's own v1 terms, element by element:

perl $KIT/bin/xmi2sysml.pl --delta ../drops/v1.0/tidewater.xmi ../drops/v1.1/tidewater.xmi

7 added, 1 changed, 0 manual: the converter carries all of it.

3. Bring the drop in. vendor/prime holds only the prime's model, converted with the repository's .ci/layout.map; git merges it into yours like two redlines of one drawing against the drawing both started from:

gl flow vendor ../drops/v1.1 v1.1

It stops on a conflict in model/physical/stations/Stations.sysml: both sides added a humidity sensor at the same place.

4. vim model/physical/stations/Stations.sysml and /<<<<<<< : each conflict shows yours (HEAD: the interim), the common base (empty) and the prime's (vendor/prime). Upstream first: the prime's model wins. Keep the prime's lines; delete yours and the four marker lines. There are two.

5. Re-apply the government's edit to the prime's new part: in part def Hygrometer replace the TODO line with @L5Assembly; then :w and

perl $KIT/tools/sysml/model.pl lint

6. Finish the merge and open the merge request; it closes the intake and DR-5, because the prime delivered what DR-5 asked for:

git add model
git commit --no-edit
gl flow finish --title "Prime drop v1.1" --description "Closes #3 and #2"

7. The pipeline fails on docs: "docs/ is stale". docs/ is generated from the model and kept in the repository, so a reviewer sees what a change does to the documents. Regenerate it, commit, push:

perl $KIT/tools/sysml/model.pl docs
git add docs
git commit -m "Regenerate docs for drop v1.1"
gl flow publish

8. Approval and merge (gl mr merge 4 names who is still needed):

gl --as jim mr approve 4
gl mr merge 4

Check: drop v1.1 on vendor/prime; a merge request from feature/drop-v1.1 that closes #3 and #2, green, approved by someone else, merged; on develop no conflict markers, no HumiditySensor, the prime's hygrometer in the sensor suite, Hygrometer tagged @L5Assembly, Bob's StationSegment tag kept.

Lesson 13: your first baseline agile-practice-13

Sandbox: lesson 12's project with drop v1.1 merged. You are Tom again: the configuration manager prepares baseline-1, the first government baseline; Jim, the MBSE lead and systems lead, approves it. (An author cannot approve their own merge request, and model/library/Interfaces.sysml needs the systems lead's approval: so the one who signs is not the one who prepares.) About 30 minutes. Task:

1. cd SANDBOX/work, source ../env.sh.

2. A release branch holds the baseline candidate while it is checked:

gl flow start release baseline-1

3. vim CHANGELOG.md: under the [Unreleased] section and above the line "[Unreleased]: ...", add the baseline's section: what it holds.

## [baseline-1] -- 2027-01-15

### Added
- Level tags on StationSegment and Hygrometer (!2, !4)

### Prime drops merged
- v1.0, 2026-10-02
- v1.1, 2027-01-08 (#3); closes DR-5 (#2)

Then:

git commit -am "CHANGELOG: baseline-1"
gl flow finish --title "Baseline 1"

4. The approvals a baseline needs: run gl mr merge 5 after each line; GitLab names who is still missing (the review rule, then the code owners of what changed since main):

gl --as jim mr approve 5
gl --as bob mr approve 5
gl mr merge 5

5. Tag it, publish the release, open the back-merge to develop:

gl flow released 5 --notes CHANGELOG.md

The tag's message carries a sha256 of docs/; the tag's own pipeline (gl pipeline list) re-checks it: the baseline is reproducible.

6. Merge the back-merge, so develop holds the baseline too:

gl --as jim mr approve 6
gl --as bob mr approve 6
gl mr merge 6
gl pages

gl pages prints where the model site is; it was rebuilt from develop.

Check: a release merge request to main, green, approved, merged; CHANGELOG.md on main has "## [baseline-1]"; tag baseline-1 on the release merge commit, with its checksum; release baseline-1; the back-merge merged and develop holding main; the model site rebuilt from develop.

17. VIM BASICS agile-vim-basics

The Vim that ships with Git for Windows is all you need. docs/VIM-CHEATSHEET.html is the one-page sheet (modes, moving, editing, search, windows, clipboard, folds, quickfix) next to the kit's own keys; vimtutor in Git Bash is a 30-minute lesson; :help is Vim's own manual. The few that matter most:

Esc            normal mode; when in doubt, press Esc
i a o          insert before, after, on a new line
:w :q :wq :q!  save, quit, both, quit without saving
u CTRL-R .     undo, redo, repeat the last change
dd yy p        delete a line, copy a line, paste
/text n        search, next
"+p "+yy       paste from / copy to the Windows clipboard
:e!            reload a file a tool rewrote
CTRL-] CTRL-O  follow a help link, come back

18. TROUBLESHOOTING agile-trouble

Every message the kit prints on an error is in the catalog, agile-errors

(vim/doc/agile-errors.txt), with what it means and the fix. Paste one:

perl agile.pl help error "PASTED MESSAGE"

When there is no message:

- A :S command does nothing or says scrum.conf is missing: you are not in a project directory. :pwd, then :cd to the project (agile-err-no-scrum-conf).

- :help agile says "Sorry, no help": the source line is not in ~/.vimrc, or vim/doc is not writable so :helptags could not run; run :helptags ~/projects/agile/vim/doc once.

- A report looks stale: daily.pl report rewrites reports/; press F5 in the browser; agile.pl rebuilds ./dashboard.html.

- Numbers look wrong: the journal is the truth. daily.pl sprint, then :SJournal and * on the task id to walk its postings.

- Mail does not open: draft, brief, cards and invite need classic Outlook on Windows (agile-err-powershell). Everything else works without it.

20. CODING DRILLS agile-drills

Interview-style coding practice in core Perl, offline, with nothing but Git for Windows: a ladder of 29 problems from trivial to hard (the binder's "Coding drills" chapter), about 130 more in technique sections (hashing, two pointers, sliding window, stacks, binary search, linked lists, trees, graphs, backtracking, dynamic programming, intervals, heaps), a four-phase drill in which the requirements change, the drill log, the refresher plan, and a Vim

memory trainer. docs/DRILLS.html is the 90-day guide.

perl drills/drill.pl next              what to do next, and why
perl drills/drill.pl start ID          your file from the stub, clock on
perl drills/drill.pl test ID           pass/fail per case, minutes so far
perl drills/drill.pl log ID NOTE       one line in the drill log

Your files, the log and the trainer's progress live in the workspace: ~/drills-work, or $DRILLS_WORK, or --dir DIR on any command. drill.pl never writes inside the kit. An ID can be shortened while it stays unique: p12 for p12-dedup, two-sum. Statements are written for this kit; a LeetCode line in each names the classic problem it resembles, as a pointer only.

The commands agile-drills-commands

drill.pl help [COMMAND] agile-drills-help

perl drills/drill.pl help, drill.pl --help This chapter, or one command's section.

drill.pl list [SECTION] agile-drills-list

Every problem by section (a section is also a trainer level): its id, the pattern, the timebox in minutes and your status (-, started, failed, passed). SECTION is a name (ladder, graphs), a prefix or a level number.

drill.pl show ID agile-drills-show

Print a problem's statement: the contract, the input and output, the edge cases worth asking about, the examples.

drill.pl start ID [--fresh] agile-drills-start

Copy the problem's stub (the signature and an empty body) to the workspace as ID.pl, record the start time, print the statement. An existing file is kept; --fresh moves it to old/ and starts again from the stub (the binder's "solve it again cold").

drill.pl test ID [FILE] [--ref] agile-drills-test

Run the problem's tests against your file (default: the workspace's ID.pl): pass or FAIL per case with the expected and actual values, the run time and the minutes since start against the timebox. Exit 0 when every case passes. Each case has a time limit (5 s); a die, an exit or an endless loop in your code fails that case, nothing more. --ref tests the reference solution. Function problems are called directly (your file defines the named sub); stdin problems run as a script with the case on stdin, and the output is compared ignoring trailing blanks, as the binder's check.sh does.

drill.pl check [SECTION | tN | ID-PREFIX] [--ref] agile-drills-check

Test every file you have in the workspace (all of them, a section, a ladder tier such as t2, or ids starting with p2): one line each, then "N passed, M failed, K not started". The binder's ./check.sh.

drill.pl solution ID [--force] agile-drills-solution

Print the reference solution with its notes: the pattern, why it works, the time and space complexity, the edge cases and the Perl idioms. Only after an attempt was recorded (start or test); --force overrides. The log counts every look (the "peeked" column of stats).

drill.pl log [ID [MINUTES] [pass|fail] [NOTES]] agile-drills-log

drill.pl log --session N With no arguments, print the drill log. With an ID, append one line "date | problem | minutes | passed | notes" to log.txt in the workspace; MINUTES defaults to the time since start, pass/fail to the last test. --session N appends the binder's session form (done, slowest thing, lookups, narration check, questions check, one thing to redo) for you to fill in with Vim. The log is append-only plain text.

drill.pl stats agile-drills-stats

Per section: problems, started, passed, peeked, minutes logged; the weakest section you have started; the log's days.

drill.pl next agile-drills-next

The refresher plan as one suggestion: a problem whose last test failed first; then the ladder in order (t0 and t1 in session 1, t2 in session 2, t3 in session 4, t4 in session 5) with the phased drill after t2 (session 3) and again after t4 (session 5); then the field drills (t5); then the weakest section; when everything passes, the problem passed longest ago, to re-solve cold (start --fresh).

drill.pl phased [N | test N [FILE] | solution] [--scenario S] agile-drills-phased

*agile-drills-phased*

The four-phase drill: one problem whose requirements change three times in an hour. With no argument, the clock plan. phased 1 prints phase 1's card, starts the clock and writes phased-SCENARIO.pl (a solve sub to fill in); read phase N+1 only when phase N passes "phased test N". phased solution is the reference, after an attempt. Scenarios: sensors (pair two sensor feeds) and payments (match orders to payments); a second run uses the other, or DRILL_SEED=99 for fresh sensor data.

The files agile-drills-files

drills/NN-SECTION/section.txt     the level's title and a line about it
drills/NN-SECTION/ID/statement.txt   header lines (Title, LeetCode, Origin,
                                  Pattern, Timebox, Kind, Call), then the
                                  contract and examples
drills/NN-SECTION/ID/tests.pl     the cases, the sample first
drills/NN-SECTION/ID/solution.pl  the reference: a comment block, then code
drills/NN-SECTION/ID/stub.pl      what start copies
drills/phased/SCENARIO/           phase1.txt..phase4.txt, data.pl (the
                                  checker), solution.pl, stub.pl
drills/toolbelt.pl                the Perl toolbelt: idioms to retype from
                                  memory, each proven
WORKSPACE/ID.pl                   your solutions
WORKSPACE/attempts.txt            start, test and solution events
WORKSPACE/log.txt                 the drill log
WORKSPACE/trainer.txt             the Vim trainer's highest unlocked level

Kinds: function (your file defines the sub named in Call), class (a package with new and the methods), stdio (a script: stdin in, stdout out). A new problem is a new directory in the same format, tests first.

The Vim trainer agile-drills-trainer

The "vanishing cues" memory game over the reference solutions. Each section is a level and each solution a card. A card shows the first line of a solution (sub two_sum {) and you type the rest. Every card is a cycle of g:drills_fade_steps reps (default 5): rep 1 shows the whole solution to copy, each later rep blanks out more of its words, the last rep shows nothing. Only that blind rep counts. A wrong answer repeats the rep; giving up on a hinted rep fades it further. A level is cleared only when every card's blind rep was right first try, which unlocks the next level; the highest unlocked level is kept in WORKSPACE/trainer.txt. Comments, blank lines, spacing and indentation are ignored when checking; the code must match. Between cards: Space or Enter continues, l chooses a level, r replays, n starts again, q quits. Settings: g:drills_work (the workspace), g:drills_fade_steps, g:drills_shuffle (0 keeps the cards in order).

:DrillTrain [N] :DrillTrain

Open the trainer at the highest unlocked level, or at level N.

:DrillLevel [N] :DrillLevel \dl

\dl                                                                      *\dl*

Choose any unlocked level (asks when N is not given).

:DrillAnswer :DrillAnswer \dc

\dc                                                                      *\dc*

Check the answer typed under the marker line (in insert mode: CTRL-G CTRL-G). Right: straight on to the next rep or card. Wrong: the solution is shown under your answer.

:DrillGiveUp :DrillGiveUp \dg

\dg                                                                      *\dg*

Show the solution. On the blind rep it counts as a miss.

:DrillNext :DrillNext \dn

\dn                                                                      *\dn*

After a miss or a level result: retry the rep, the next rep, the next card, the level result or the next level (Space and Enter do the same).

\dr \dr

Replay the current level from its first card.

:DrillQuit :DrillQuit \dq

\dq                                                                      *\dq*

Leave the trainer. Cleared levels are already saved.

:DrillReset :DrillReset

Forget all progress: only level 1 is unlocked again (asks first).

:DrillOpen :DrillOpen \do

\do                                                                      *\do*

Jump between a problem's statement (drills/.../statement.txt) and your file in the workspace. The first time, drill.pl start makes the file and starts the clock.

:DrillTest :DrillTest \dt

\dt                                                                      *\dt*

Save and run drill.pl test on this problem; the result opens in a split.

:DrillTestAll [SECTION | tN] :DrillTestAll \da

\da                                                                      *\da*

drill.pl check: every file you have in the workspace, in a split.

21. GITLAB, GITFLOW AND THE PIPELINE agile-gitlab

The model team's GitLab work from the command line, offline or against a server. gitlab.pl talks to a GitLab server (--url, with a token) or to the offline emulator in a folder (--local DIR), which behaves like GitLab: it enforces protected branches and tags, code-owner approvals and "pipelines must succeed", runs the project's .gitlab-ci.yml, and merges with real merge commits. Everything here is core Perl and needs only Git for Windows. Guide: docs/GITLAB.html. Messages: agile-errors-gitlab.

gitlab.pl agile-gitlab-pl

    perl bin/gitlab.pl [--url URL [--token-env VAR] | --local DIR]
                       [--project GROUP/NAME] [--as USER] [--now ISO] [--dry-run] COMMAND
setup FILE              apply a project file (tools/gitlab/templates/project.conf):
                        settings, members, labels, sprints, protected branches
                        and tags, approval rules, variables, schedules; safe to
                        run again
setup --diff FILE       compare the project file with the live project, read
                        only; prints each difference; exit 1 on drift
sprints START COUNT     "Sprint N" milestones, two weeks each (--weeks, --prefix)
issue new|list|show|close|reopen|note|link|label    issues; new takes
                        --template NAME (from .gitlab/issue_templates); notes
                        may carry quick actions (/label, /milestone, /estimate)
mr new|list|show|approve|merge|note|resolve         merge requests; show prints
                        the pipeline, approvals and the report widgets
pipeline run|list|show  pipelines and their jobs
tag, release            annotated tags (protected baseline-* need a maintainer)
                        and releases with Markdown notes
wiki put|list|show      wiki pages from Markdown files
export DIR              CSVs for status metrics: ci_jobs, mrs, issues, defects,
                        tracker/sprint-N
package put|get|list    the Generic Package Registry (prime drops, baselines),
                        checked by sha256
pages, env              where the GitLab Pages model site is; environments and
                        deployments
schedule new|list|run|delete|due|next   cron pipeline schedules; next previews a
                        cron line: schedule next "0 2 * * 1-5" --tz America/New_York
analytics               value stream, DORA in model terms, CI/CD, merge request
                        and issue analytics, from data any tier exposes
                        (--by sprint|week|month, --csv DIR)
trigger new|list|run    pipeline trigger tokens (the prime's Jenkins starts the
                        intake pipeline with DROP_VERSION)
token deploy new|list   deploy tokens limited to scopes, with an expiry date
user USERNAME           create a user (emulator, or an admin token)
ci                      run the pipeline locally: agile-gitlab-ci
flow                    gitflow in a clone: agile-gitlab-flow
help [COMMAND]          the full option list of one command

--dry-run prints each request that would change something and changes nothing; reads still answer (both backends; flow refuses it). Environment: GITLAB_URL, GITLAB_LOCAL, GITLAB_PROJECT, GITLAB_USER, GITLAB_TOKEN.

gitlab.pl flow agile-gitlab-flow

Gitflow for the model repository: main holds released baselines, develop is the integration branch (GitLab's default branch), work happens on feature/ branches, baselines on release/ branches, fixes to a baseline on hotfix/ branches, and every prime drop lands on vendor/prime, never edited by hand.

flow init                     develop from main
flow start feature|release|hotfix NAME   a branch from develop (hotfix: main)
flow publish                  push the current branch
flow finish [--title T] [--template NAME] [--label L]...   push and open the
                              merge request (feature -> develop; release and
                              hotfix -> main)
flow released IID             after a release merge request merged: tag main
                              (the docs' sha256 in the message), release,
                              back-merge merge request to develop
flow vendor DROPDIR VERSION [--layout-map FILE]   commit the converted prime
                              drop on vendor/prime and merge it into
                              feature/drop-VERSION; conflicts are listed

flow take ours|theirs PATH... resolve conflicted files wholesale

flow sync                     fetch; fast-forward local main and develop

gitlab.pl ci agile-gitlab-ci

perl bin/gitlab.pl ci [--file .gitlab-ci.yml] [--event push|merge_request_event|tag|schedule|web|trigger]
                      [--branch B] [--target B] [--tag T] [--var K=V]... [--job NAME]... [--manual] [--list]

Runs the project's pipeline here, offline, choosing jobs as GitLab would for that event (rules, only/except, workflow, extends, local includes); --list shows the jobs and why the others are skipped, without running anything. Includes of GitLab's own templates and of other projects are listed as "runs on GitLab only".

ci/job.pl agile-ci-job

perl ci/job.pl NAME

Every job of the model pipeline is one line, perl ci/job.pl NAME, so the same .gitlab-ci.yml runs under PowerShell, Git Bash and Docker. Jobs: grammar, lint, outline, todo, secrets, trace, vcrm, recipe, complexity, docs, delta, drop-package, intake, baseline, publish-package, publish-release, pages, status, sil-regression, hil-test. It finds the kit through the CI/CD variable KIT and checks it against .kit-version. The trace, outline and complexity jobs are ratchets: a merge request fails only when it makes things worse.

kickoff.pl agile-kickoff

perl tools/gitlab/kickoff.pl doctor [--quick] [--fix]
perl tools/gitlab/kickoff.pl scaffold DIR [--project G/N] [--title T] [--levels L1A,L2B,...]
perl tools/gitlab/kickoff.pl start [--yes] [--local DIR | --url URL] [--drop DIR --version V] [--from N]

Week zero for a model team. doctor checks the laptop (Perl, git and its settings, Vim, curl, a quick self-test, GitLab, an SSH key) and prints the fix for each problem; --fix sets only the recommended git settings. scaffold makes the model repository from tools/gitlab/templates in an empty folder. start runs the week-zero steps in order, each only with --yes.

talk.pl agile-talk

perl tools/gitlab/talk.pl standup --as USER | review --sprint N | weekly | translate FILE

Drafts words from GitLab and the journal, never posts: a terse Y/T/B line (outcome first, one number), a sprint-review demo script with the four headline numbers, a weekly note for management, or a jargon list with "so what?" flags for a draft you wrote.

ci-reports.pl, req-recipe.pl, memo-build.pl agile-team-tools

perl tools/gitlab/ci-reports.pl grammar|lint|outline|todo|trace [--junit F] [--codequality F] [--metrics F] LOG
perl tools/sysml/req-recipe.pl [--format text|csv|junit|codequality] [--strict] INPUT...
perl tools/memo/memo-build.pl [--check] FILE.md...

ci-reports turns a checker's output into GitLab's merge-request reports. req-recipe grades requirement statements against the requirement recipe (the 18-part single sentence) in .sysml, DOORS or text. memo-build renders a memo written from the templates in tools/gitlab/templates/memos/ (through md2memo.pl, agile-memo) and reports blanks still to fill.

vim:tw=78:ts=8:ft=help:norl:

1. PROJECT AND FILES agile-errors

no scrum.conf found here or above (run: daily.pl init) agile-err-no-scrum-conf

Pattern: no scrum.conf found here or above Pattern: has no scrum.conf (run daily.pl init there first) Pattern: no such project directory Pattern: no scrum.conf here or above Pattern: no such file: *

From:    daily.pl (any command), agile.pl, the :S commands, sim/rehearsal.pl
Means:   The command looks for scrum.conf in the current directory and
         every directory above it, and found none (or -c named a file
         that does not exist, or agile.pl was given a directory that is
         not a project).
Fix:     cd into the project first (the directory daily.pl init made, or
         any directory below it), or pass -c PATH/scrum.conf. For
         agile.pl, give the project path: perl agile.pl ~/scrum/myprogram.
         No project yet: daily.pl init DIR (agile-first-project).
         In Vim, :pwd shows where you are; :cd to the project.

cannot write FILE: REASON agile-err-cannot-write

Pattern: cannot write *: * Pattern: cannot append *: * Pattern: cannot append to *: * Pattern: help: cannot write *: * Pattern: idef0: cannot write *: * Pattern: cannot write devsecops.html: * Pattern: drill: cannot write *: *

From:    daily.pl (report, review, rollup, csv, drill, propose, lint,
         answers, cards, init), agile.pl, scrum.pl, Roster.pm, Ai.pm,
         Attendance.pm, Calendar.pm, Standup.pm, idef0.pl fmt --write
Means:   The file could not be opened for writing. REASON is the system's
         words: "Permission denied" (read-only, or open and locked in
         another program: Excel holds a CSV open, OneDrive or antivirus is
         syncing it), "No such file or directory" (the directory is
         missing), "No space left on device".
Fix:     Close the file in Excel or the browser, wait for OneDrive, check
         the directory exists and is yours (ls -ld DIR), then run the
         command again. Reports are regenerated every time, so nothing is
         lost by re-running.

cannot read FILE: REASON / cannot open FILE: REASON agile-err-cannot-read

Pattern: cannot read *: * Pattern: cannot open *: * Pattern: help: cannot read *: * Pattern: idef0: cannot read *: [Errno * Pattern: cannot read logo *: *

From:    daily.pl (chat, answers, lint, attend, drill --grade), chat.pl,
         cal.pl, Ledger.pm, Standup.pm, Answers.pm, Attendance.pm,
         Calendar.pm (calendar_fixture), idef0.pl
Means:   The named file is missing or cannot be read: a typo in the path,
         a file not yet created (today's chat before you pasted it), or a
         scrum.conf key (journal, calendar_fixture) pointing nowhere.
Fix:     ls the path. Paths in scrum.conf are relative to scrum.conf.
         For today's chat: :SChat creates it, paste, :w.

cannot chdir DIR: REASON agile-err-cannot-chdir

Pattern: cannot chdir *: *

From:    daily.pl, daily.pl init, devsecops.pl
Means:   The project (or kit) directory cannot be entered: removed,
         renamed, or on a drive that is not connected.
Fix:     Check the path (ls -ld DIR). Reconnect the share, or run init
         with a directory you own.

commands: init new status compile report ... agile-err-daily-commands

Pattern: commands: init new status compile report draft brief commit

From:    daily.pl
Means:   The command word is not one daily.pl knows (a typo, or an
         option before the command that needs a value: -c FILE).
Fix:     The list printed is every command. daily.pl help COMMAND for
         one; perl agile.pl help search WORD to find it (agile-daily).

unknown command 'X' (sprint velocity backlog ...) agile-err-unknown-command

Pattern: unknown command '*' (sprint velocity Pattern: unknown command '*' (bal reg Pattern: idef0: unknown command *

From:    scrum.pl, ledger.pl, idef0.pl
Means:   The first word after the options is not a command of that tool.
Fix:     The parentheses list every command. scrum.pl help, ledger.pl
         help (agile-scrum, agile-ledger, agile-idef0-commands).

usage: ... agile-err-usage

Pattern: usage: daily.pl rollup [YYYY-MM] Pattern: usage: daily.pl roster add "Name" email Team "Role" "Org" Pattern: --until wants YYYY-MM-DD Pattern: usage: perl agile.pl help search WORDS Pattern: usage: perl agile.pl help error Pattern: usage: docs2txt.pl grep [-i] PATTERN FILE... Pattern: -o needs a directory Pattern: usage: idef0 svg NODE FILE... Pattern: usage: md2memo.pl Pattern: --banner must be page or doc Pattern: --font must be times or courier Pattern: usage: perl agile.pl practice

From:    daily.pl rollup, roster add, invite; agile.pl help; docs2txt.pl;
         idef0.pl svg; md2memo.pl; agile.pl practice
Means:   An argument is missing or in the wrong form; the message shows
         the right form.
Fix:     Run it again as shown. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, months YYYY-MM.
         Quote names with spaces: roster add "Lee, Ann" ...

2. COMPILING A STAND-UP FILE agile-errors-compile

A stand-up file is checked whole: every error in it is listed, and nothing from it is applied until all are fixed. Fix the lines, :SDry until clean, then :SCompile. Each message starts with the file (and line).

FILE: NOT applied agile-err-not-applied

Pattern: : NOT applied

From:    daily.pl compile (and all, :SCompile)
Means:   The stand-up file named has at least one error (listed under
         this line) and none of it went into the journal. Files after it
         were not tried either.
Fix:     Look each listed error up (they are below), fix the file, then
         daily.pl --dry compile until it prints no errors, then compile.
         Runbook: agile-howto-bad-compile.

FILE:LINE: unknown verb 'X' agile-err-unknown-verb

Pattern: unknown verb '*'

From:    Standup.pm (compile, --dry compile)
Means:   The first word of the line is not a verb: a typo (don, comit),
         a sentence typed as a line, or a status pasted without ; in
         front.
Fix:     Use a verb from agile-verbs, or put ; before free text, or
         write it as note TEXT.

FILE:LINE: 'VERB' needs a team section (== Team) first agile-err-needs-team

Pattern: needs a team section (== Team) first

From:    Standup.pm
Means:   A verb line comes before any "== Team" header (or after a bare
         "==" that ended the section). Only note and risk may stand
         outside a section.
Fix:     Add "== Team" above the line (the team's exact name, as in
         daily.pl sprint), or "== Master" for the master backlog.

FILE:LINE: VERB needs an id (and other missing arguments) agile-err-verb-args

Pattern: hold needs an id Pattern: punt needs an id Pattern: redo needs an id Pattern: commit needs an id Pattern: block needs an id Pattern: refine needs an id Pattern: prune needs an id Pattern: pass needs id and the receiving team Pattern: sync needs two or more ids Pattern: assign needs id and owner Pattern: est needs id and points Pattern: cap needs a number Pattern: new needs: id points title

From:    Standup.pm
Means:   The verb is right but its arguments are not: a missing id, a
         missing owner or team, points that are not a number (est A-1
         five), or new without points (new A-1 Title).
Fix:     The forms are in agile-verbs: new ID PTS TITLE [p:N e:EPIC
         t:TOME o:OWNER], est ID PTS, assign ID OWNER, pass ID TEAM,
         sync ID ID, cap N. Quote multi-word values: o:"Bob Ray".

FILE: no date (put YYYY-MM-DD in the file name or on the first line) agile-err-no-date

Pattern: no date (put YYYY-MM-DD in the file name or on the first line)

From:    Standup.pm
Means:   The stand-up file's name has no date and no line of the file is
         a bare date.
Fix:     Name it standups/YYYY-MM-DD.txt (daily.pl new does), or put the
         date alone on the first line.

FILE: no sprint number (add 'sprint N') agile-err-no-sprint

Pattern: no sprint number (add 'sprint N')

From:    Standup.pm
Means:   The journal has no sprint yet and the file does not say which
         sprint it is (a new project's first file).
Fix:     Put "sprint 1" on the line after the date (agile-verb-sprint).

FILE: unknown task 'ID' agile-err-unknown-task

Pattern: unknown task '*'

From:    Standup.pm
Means:   No task with that id is in the journal, nor created earlier in
         this file. Usually a typo (B-12 for B-121), or the new line for
         it is in a later file.
Fix:     daily.pl backlog TEAM or :SJournal and /ID to find the right id.
         In Vim, CTRL-X CTRL-K completes ids from the journal. To create
         it: new ID PTS TITLE in this file.

FILE: task 'ID' already exists agile-err-task-exists

Pattern: task '*' already exists

From:    Standup.pm (new, new!)
Means:   A new line uses an id that is already in the journal (or twice
         in this file). Ids are never reused, even for removed tasks.
Fix:     Pick a new id. To bring an existing task into the sprint use
         commit; to resize it use est.

FILE: 'ID' is not committed in sprint N for TEAM (at: ACCOUNTS) agile-err-not-committed

Pattern: is not committed in sprint * for *

From:    Standup.pm (done, carry, drop, punt, pass)
Means:   These verbs move a task out of this sprint's Committed account
         for this team, and the task is not there. "at:" says where its
         points are: a backlog (commit it first), Done (already done),
         Carryover, another team's sprint (wrong section), or "nowhere"
         (removed). A "sprint N" line for the wrong sprint does this to
         every line.
Fix:     Put the line under the right "== Team"; check the file's sprint
         number; daily.pl sprint shows what is committed. For a task in
         a backlog use commit first; to retire it from a backlog use
         prune.

FILE: 'ID' is not in a backlog or carryover for TEAM (at: ACCOUNTS) agile-err-not-in-backlog

Pattern: is not in a backlog or carryover for * Pattern: is not in the master backlog or another team's backlog Pattern: is not in a backlog (at: *); use drop for committed work

From:    Standup.pm (commit, refine, prune)
Means:   commit takes a task from the team's backlog, the master backlog
         or a past sprint's Carryover; refine from the master or another
         team's backlog; prune from a backlog. The task is elsewhere,
         shown after "at:" (already committed, done, removed).
Fix:     Already in the sprint: nothing to do. Committed work you want
         out: drop (or carry). A task of another team: refine it into
         this team's backlog first, or put the line under that team.

FILE: 'ID' has no points to re-estimate agile-err-no-points

Pattern: has no points to re-estimate

From:    Standup.pm (est)
Means:   The task has no points anywhere (done and closed, or removed),
         so there is nothing to resize.
Fix:     Estimate open work only. To change history, post a new task.

FILE: 'ID' is not Done for TEAM in any sprint (at: ...); redo is for finished work agile-err-redo-not-done

Pattern: is not Done for * in any sprint

From:    Standup.pm (redo)
Means:   redo brings a task that was done back into this sprint; this
         one was never done for this team.
Fix:     For work still committed, nothing is needed; for another team's
         task put the line under that team.

FILE is already in JOURNAL: marked it compiled, applied nothing agile-err-already-compiled

Pattern: is already in *: marked it compiled, applied nothing

From:    Standup.pm (compile)
Means:   An earlier compile appended this file's entries but could not
         mark the file (it was locked). The kit noticed and did not apply
         it twice. A warning, not an error.
Fix:     Nothing. To change what it did, see agile-howto-bad-compile.

writing JOURNAL failed (...): check the end of the journal ... agile-err-journal-write-failed

Pattern: failed (*): check the end of the journal before compiling again Pattern: cannot mark * compiled (*); it is applied

From:    Standup.pm (compile)
Means:   The disk was full or the journal (or stand-up file) was locked
         by another program while compile wrote it. The first message:
         the journal may end with a partial entry and the stand-up file is
         NOT marked compiled. The second: the entries are in, the mark is
         not; the next compile notices.
Fix:     Close what holds the file (an editor, OneDrive). After the first
         message, git diff scrum.txt: remove a partial last entry (or git
         checkout -- scrum.txt), then compile again.

3. THE JOURNAL AND LEDGER FILES agile-errors-ledger

FILE:LINE: unrecognised line / bad date / bad amount ... agile-err-journal-line

Pattern: unexpected indented line Pattern: bad date '*' Pattern: cannot include '*': * Pattern: unrecognised line: * Pattern: bad amount '*' Pattern: bad price '*'

From:    Ledger.pm (every command that reads the journal: daily.pl
         status and all others, scrum.pl, ledger.pl)
Means:   A line of the journal (usually a hand edit) does not parse:
         a posting not under a dated transaction line, a date not
         YYYY-MM-DD, an amount that is not a number with a unit, a single
         space between account and amount (two or more are needed).
Fix:     Open the file at the line (vim +LINE scrum.txt), compare with the
         lines around it, fix it, then daily.pl status. If you did not
         edit it: git diff scrum.txt; git checkout -- scrum.txt.

FILE:LINE: transaction does not balance (off by N) agile-err-unbalanced

Pattern: transaction does not balance (off by *) Pattern: more than one posting without an amount

From:    Ledger.pm
Means:   The postings of an entry do not sum to zero, or two postings
         leave their amount out (only one may).
Fix:     Make the amounts sum to zero, or leave exactly one amount out
         (it balances the rest). In the scrum journal every move is a
