         pair: -5 SP out of one account, 5 SP into another.

bad period 'X' (want YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-Qn) agile-err-bad-period

Pattern: bad period '*' (want YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-Qn) Pattern: budget: need period or begin+end Pattern: bad --begin Pattern: bad --end Pattern: bad --now (want YYYY-MM-DD)

From:    ledger.pl
Means:   A date option is not in a form ledger.pl reads.
Fix:     -p 2026, -p 2026-09 or -p 2026-Q3; -b and -e and --now take
         YYYY-MM-DD.

evm: budget '~ ...' (FILE:LINE) needs 'from DATE to DATE' ... agile-err-evm-budget

Pattern: needs 'from DATE to DATE' to give a budget at completion

From:    ledger.pl evm
Means:   Earned value needs time-phased budgets: a "~ Monthly" entry with
         no window has no budget at completion.
Fix:     Write the budget as ~ Monthly from 2026-10-01 to 2027-01-01
         (agile-howto-funding).

percent complete for 'ACCOUNT' is not a number / is over 100 agile-err-complete

Pattern: percent complete for '*' is not a number Pattern: percent complete for '*' is over 100 Pattern: --complete wants ACCOUNT=PCT, got '*' Pattern: want 'account,pct'

From:    ledger.pl evm (--complete, --complete-file)
Means:   A percent-complete value is malformed: not a number, over 100,
         an option without "=", or a CSV line that is not "account,pct".
Fix:     --complete Expense:Labor=40 (also 0.4 or 40%); CSV lines like
         Expense:Labor,40 (a header line and # comments are fine).

csv: unknown table 'X' (items sprints epics intake health) agile-err-csv-table

Pattern: csv: unknown table '*'

From:    daily.pl csv, scrum.pl csv
Means:   The table name is not one of the list.
Fix:     Use one of the names shown; daily.pl csv with no name writes all.

4. THE CHAT, LINT AND ANSWERS agile-errors-chat

lint prints FILE:LINE: ERROR|warn|ok Name: reason. ERROR: the status cannot be used; warn: it parses but tells the kit little. The fix is the person's repost, prompted by lint --reply (agile-ytb).

ERROR Name: no Y/T/B found / no B found agile-err-lint-no-ytb

Pattern: no Y/T/B found Pattern: no * found

From:    Answers.pm (lint, answers)
Means:   The person's message has no Y, T and B delimiters at all, or
         lacks one of them ("no B found": they left out the blockers).
Fix:     Reply with the format: Y did B-11 T doing B-12 B none. "B none"
         is data. A repost replaces the first message.

ERROR Name: 'B' appears 2 times: capitalize the one that is the delimiter agile-err-lint-dup-delim

Pattern: appears * times: capitalize the one that is the delimiter

From:    Answers.pm
Means:   Lowercase y t b are accepted only when unambiguous; here a letter
         occurs twice ("will b in the lab"), so the kit will not guess.
         lint --reply offers its best reading as "Did you mean ...?".
Fix:     The person reposts with capital Y T B, or thumbs-up the "did you
         mean"; then daily.pl answers --guess takes that reading.

ERROR Name: T is empty; B is empty (write 'none') agile-err-lint-empty

Pattern: is empty (write 'none') Pattern: * is empty

From:    Answers.pm (lint, answers)
Means:   The delimiters are there but a field has nothing after it: only
         "Y: ..." was posted, or "B" with nothing. A blocker field must
         say none when there is none.
Fix:     The person reposts all three: Y did B-11 T doing B-12 B none.

ERROR Name: out of order: expected Y ... T ... B ... agile-err-lint-order

Pattern: out of order: expected Y ... T ... B ...

From:    Answers.pm
Means:   All three delimiters are there but not in the order Y, T, B.
Fix:     Repost in order.

warn Name: no task id in Y (e.g. B-11) / ID is not in the journal agile-err-lint-no-id

Pattern: no task id in * (e.g. *) Pattern: * is not in the journal

From:    Answers.pm
Means:   The status parses, but Y or T names no task id, so it cannot be
         tied to the journal; or an id is not in the journal (a typo).
Fix:     lint --reply says "Add the task id next time" or "X isn't in the
         backlog -- typo?". A warning does not stop answers.

no chat file for DATE / no chat files for DATE / no Y/T/B answers found agile-err-no-chat-file

Pattern: no chat file Pattern: no chat files for * Pattern: no Y/T/B answers found Pattern: no #est / #vote markers Pattern: no answers files for * Pattern: no attendance reports for *

From:    daily.pl lint, answers, chat, ai, joined
Means:   Today's input file is not there yet, or it holds no statuses or
         rounds. The file names are standups/DATE-chat.txt (or
         DATE-TEAM-chat.txt) for the chat and
         standups/DATE[-TEAM]-attendance.csv for the attendance download.
Fix:     :SChat, paste the Teams chat (CTRL-A CTRL-C there), :w. For ai,
         run answers first. --today D if you are catching up a past day.

chat: no team for est lines of tasks not in the journal yet agile-err-chat-no-team

Pattern: chat: no team for est lines of tasks not in the journal yet: *

From:    daily.pl chat
Means:   A round estimated a task the journal does not have yet. Its est
         line (commented) went under a bare "==", which ends every team
         section, so uncommenting it would fail the compile with "'est'
         needs a team section". There was no team to put it under: no
         default_team in scrum.conf and no team in the file name.
Fix:     Set default_team = TEAM in scrum.conf, or name the chat file
         standups/DATE-TEAM-chat.txt, and run the tally again; or move the
         lines under "== TEAM" by hand before you uncomment them.

NAME owns tasks in the journal but is not in roster.txt (roster check) agile-err-roster-check

Pattern: owns tasks in the journal but is not in roster.txt Pattern: roster team '*' differs from the journal's '*' Pattern: is in roster.txt but owns no task in the journal Pattern: no e-mail (1:1 links and the invite will skip them) Pattern: *: no team Pattern: * appears twice (lines * Pattern: no e-mails in roster.txt

From:    daily.pl roster, invite
Means:   roster.txt and the journal disagree: an owner's name is spelled
         differently (it must be the Teams display name, exactly), a
         person's team changed, a line has no e-mail, or a name is listed
         twice.
Fix:     daily.pl roster add "Name" email Team Role Org updates a line; or
         edit roster.txt (Name | email | Team | Role | Org). To fix the
         journal side: assign ID "Right Name" in a stand-up file.

5. MAIL, CALENDAR, AI agile-errors-mail

refusing: fix the marking errors above, or run again with --force agile-err-marking-refused

Pattern: refusing: fix the marking errors above Pattern: error: recipient * is outside mail_domains

From:    daily.pl draft, brief, cards --send/--draft, invite, check
Means:   scrum.conf sets mail_domains and a recipient (to, cc, an
         attendee) is outside them. Nothing was opened or sent.
Fix:     Correct the address in scrum.conf (to, cc) or roster.txt, or the
         mail_domains list; daily.pl check to confirm. --force only if
         you are sure the recipient may receive the material.

warn: marking_owner is empty ... (marking advisories) agile-err-marking-warn

Pattern: warn: marking_owner is empty Pattern: warn: marking_poc is empty Pattern: warn: subject_prefix is empty while a banner is set

From:    daily.pl check, draft, brief, cards, invite
Means:   A banner is set but the marking block is incomplete. Advisory:
         mail still goes.
Fix:     Fill marking_owner, marking_poc and subject_prefix in scrum.conf
         (agile-conf-banner).

powershell.exe failed (is this Windows with Outlook installed?) agile-err-powershell

Pattern: powershell.exe failed (is this Windows with Outlook installed?) Pattern: powershell failed (rc=*) Pattern: bad JSON from PowerShell Pattern: cannot run *: * Pattern: create: need subject and start Pattern: post needs an event id or subject pattern Pattern: no event matching '*' Pattern: commands: list dump attend

From:    daily.pl draft, brief, cards, invite, attend, post, meetings;
         scrum.pl draft; cal.pl
Means:   The Outlook steps drive classic Outlook through PowerShell COM.
         This fails when not on Windows, with "new Outlook" (it has no
         COM), with Outlook not set up, or when a policy blocks it.
Fix:     On Windows, open classic Outlook once and try again. Offline or
         elsewhere set calendar = mock and calendar_fixture = FILE.json in
         scrum.conf for the calendar steps, and send mail by pasting
         reports/DATE-status.html. docs/TEST-PLAN.html is the 30-minute
         check of this layer on a laptop.

AI request failed: ... / unknown ai_backend / ai_url not set agile-err-ai

Pattern: AI request failed: * Pattern: unknown ai_backend '*' Pattern: ai_url not set in scrum.conf Pattern: cannot run curl: * Pattern: curl failed (rc=*): * Pattern: bad JSON from AI endpoint: * Pattern: no text in AI response: *

From:    daily.pl ai
Means:   With ai_backend = curl the kit calls an OpenAI-style endpoint
         through Git's curl; the call failed (no network, wrong URL, a
         key variable not set, a proxy) or the reply was not the expected
         JSON.
Fix:     Use ai_backend = paste (the default): daily.pl ai writes the
         prompt, you paste it into the approved service and save the reply
         as reports/DATE-ai-response.txt. Nothing else depends on the AI.
         Otherwise check ai_url, ai_model and ai_key_env (agile-conf-ai_url).

not a git repository (git init first) agile-err-not-git

Pattern: not a git repository (git init first)

From:    daily.pl commit, all
Means:   The project directory is not a git repository (made by hand, or
         copied without .git).
Fix:     In the project: git init, git config core.autocrlf false, then
         daily.pl commit (agile-howto-backup).

6. THE KIT'S OTHER TOOLS agile-errors-tools

FILE: TOOL not found / no converter for .EXT agile-err-docs2txt

Pattern: not found (Git for Windows ships it in mingw64/bin or usr/bin) Pattern: no converter for .* Pattern: failed on *

From:    docs2txt.pl, :SDocs
Means:   The converter for that format (pdftotext, docx2txt, antiword,
         odt2txt) is not on this machine, or it failed on the file (a
         scanned PDF has no text).
Fix:     perl bin/docs2txt.pl tools shows which were found. Git for
         Windows ships them; a minimal Git install may not.

working tree not clean: commit first agile-err-release

Pattern: working tree not clean: commit first Pattern: git tag failed Pattern: git archive failed

From:    release.pl
Means:   A release is built from a commit, so uncommitted changes stop
         it; or the tag already exists.
Fix:     git status; commit or stash; use a new tag name.

daily.pl report failed / cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:PORT agile-err-report-failed

Pattern: daily.pl report failed Pattern: cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:*: *

From:    agile.pl, agile.pl serve
Means:   The report step for the cockpit failed (its own message is
         above this one), or the port is in use (serve is already
         running in another window).
Fix:     Run daily.pl report in the project to see the error. For serve:
         close the other one, or --port 8091.

bad classification 'X' agile-err-memo

Pattern: bad classification '*'

From:    md2memo.pl
Means:   A marking tag {X}...{/} uses a class md2memo does not know.
Fix:     Classes are U, CUI, C, S, TS, with controls after //:
         {S//NF}...{/}. Write a literal brace as \{.

practice: no lesson N / lesson N is not set up agile-err-practice

Pattern: practice: no lesson * Pattern: practice: lesson * is not set up Pattern: practice: lesson * needs * Pattern: practice: *

From:    agile.pl practice
Means:   The lesson number is not in the list, its sandbox has not been
         made yet (run practice N first), or a lesson needs a tool or file
         that is not in this copy of the kit.
Fix:     perl agile.pl practice lists the lessons; practice N sets one up;
         practice reset N starts it over.

release: no profile 'NAME' / a manifest line names a missing file agile-err-release-profile

Pattern: release: --list needs --profile NAME Pattern: release: a profile name is letters, digits, _ and - ('*') Pattern: release: no profile '*' (*: *) Pattern: release: * names files that are not in the tree: *

From:    release.pl --profile NAME, --list
Means:   A profile release packs only the files
         tools/gitlab/NAME-release.txt lists (one path or glob per line; a
         line starting with ? is optional). --list was given without a
         profile, the profile name has other characters, there is no
         manifest for that name, or a required line matches no committed
         file.
Fix:     perl bin/release.pl --profile mbse --list shows what the mbse
         profile packs. Commit the missing file, remove its line, or mark it
         optional with ? at the start of the line. Profile names are
         letters, digits, _ and -.

memo-build: FILE: no "## Subject: ..." line / placeholders to fill in agile-err-memo-build

Pattern: usage: memo-build.pl * Pattern: memo-build: unknown option * Pattern: no "## Memorandum for ..." line Pattern: no "## From: ..." line Pattern: no "## Subject: ..." line Pattern: * placeholder(s) to fill in: * Pattern: * TODO-SIM marker(s): numbers still to come from the simulation's evidence Pattern: memo-build: *: warning: * Pattern: memo-build: *: *

From:    tools/memo/memo-build.pl (the memo templates in
         tools/gitlab/templates/memos/)
Means:   memo-build strips the template's comments, checks the header lines
         md2memo needs (## Memorandum for, ## From:, ## Subject:) and warns
         about blanks still written as <<...>> or TODO-SIM; with --check it
         renders nothing and exits 1 when a blank is left. The last form is
         md2memo's own failure, or a file it cannot read or write.
Fix:     Start from a template (docs/memos/templates/ in a repo made by
         kickoff.pl scaffold), keep its ## header lines, fill every <<...>>,
         then perl $KIT/tools/memo/memo-build.pl --check FILE.md. md2memo
         options go after --. A read or write error names the path: check
         it.

pages-index: DIR is not a directory / mkguide: guide.html.in must start with <!DOCTYPE html> agile-err-pages-index

Pattern: usage: pages-index.pl * Pattern: pages-index: * is not a directory Pattern: mkguide: guide.html.in must start with <!DOCTYPE html>

From:    tools/gitlab/pages-index.pl (the pipeline's pages job),
         tools/gitlab/mkguide.pl (rebuilds docs/GITLAB.html)
Means:   pages-index writes the front page of the model site into an
         existing folder (public/), so the folder must exist first. mkguide
         found a damaged guide source.
Fix:     In the pages job, the views and documents are copied into public/
         before pages-index runs: run perl ci/job.pl pages, not pages-index
         alone. For mkguide: git checkout -- tools/gitlab/guide.html.in.

7. IDEF0 MODELS agile-errors-idef0

idef0.pl lint prints FILE:LINE: error: ... or warning: ...; in Vim the list is the quickfix list (\il, then :cn).

tabs in indentation; use 2 spaces per level agile-err-idef0-tabs

Pattern: tabs in indentation; use 2 spaces per level Pattern: indentation of * is not a multiple of * Pattern: indentation jumps from level * to *

From:    idef0.pl lint
Means:   Nesting is by indentation, two spaces per level: a tab, an odd
         number of spaces, or a child indented two levels below its
         parent.
Fix:     In Vim the IDEF0 buffer uses 2-space indents: >> and << shift by
         one level; :retab turns tabs into spaces.

cannot parse line / line has no name / no parent agile-err-idef0-parse

Pattern: cannot parse line: * Pattern: line has no name Pattern: line has no parent model/activity Pattern: not allowed in a name (link paths follow < or >) Pattern: empty segment in link path Pattern: model root 't' must be at indentation 0 Pattern: activity nested under a port Pattern: port nested under a port

From:    idef0.pl lint
Means:   A line is not "TAG# Name [> or < link]" (tags: t model, a
         activity, i c o m ports), a name is missing, a line is nested
         under a port, a name holds a | (only link paths use |), or the
         model line is indented.
Fix:     Compare with a line that lints: "  a# Define Quad Spec",
         "    o# Quad Spec > F|Cut Frame Parts|Quad Spec".

outputs declare goes-to with '>', not '<' agile-err-idef0-direction

Pattern: outputs declare goes-to with '>', not '<' Pattern: ports declare comes-from with '<', not '>' Pattern: link source '*' is '*' -- flows must originate at an output Pattern: link destination '*' is an output

From:    idef0.pl lint
Means:   An output (o) says where its flow goes with >; an input,
         control or mechanism (i c m) says where it comes from with <.
         A flow starts at an output and ends at an i, c or m.
Fix:     Flip the arrow, or move the link to the other end of the flow.

broken link: cannot resolve 'A|B|Flow' agile-err-idef0-broken-link

Pattern: broken link: cannot resolve '*' Pattern: has no unique port for flow '*'; add the port or use o1/i1 form Pattern: one-sided cross-model link: * Pattern: has no producer; did you mean '*'? Pattern: has no consumer; did you mean '*'?

From:    idef0.pl lint
Means:   A link path names a model, activity or flow that is not there
         (spelling, or the other model was not linted with this one), an
         activity has two ports for the flow, a cross-model link is
         declared on one side only, or a flow is produced or consumed
         nowhere.
Fix:     Lint the whole project together (\iL, or idef0.pl lint
         model/*.txt) so cross-model links resolve; fix the spelling the
         message suggests; add the reciprocal < or > on the other side.
         \if jumps to a link's target.

bad suffix / duplicate model letter / more than 9 activities agile-err-idef0-numbering

Pattern: bad model suffix *: use a single letter or # Pattern: duplicate model letter '*' (also *) Pattern: more than 9 activities on one plate Pattern: pinned number * must be a single digit 1-9 Pattern: duplicate pinned digit * on plate * (also line *) Pattern: bad activity suffix * Pattern: asserted number * but position derives * Pattern: asserted numbers are for activities; ports take # or a digit Pattern: pinned port number * must be a single digit 1-9 Pattern: bad port suffix *

From:    idef0.pl lint, fmt
Means:   The character after the tag letter is the number: # derives it
         from position, a digit pins it. Models need distinct letters; a
         plate holds at most nine activities.
Fix:     Use # unless you mean to pin (\iu, fmt --auto, resets them);
         split a plate with more than nine children one level down.

unclosed ```idef0 fence / doc comment / no plate / fmt refusing agile-err-idef0-other

Pattern: unclosed ```idef0 fence at end of file Pattern: doc comment has no element line to attach to Pattern: idef0: no plate * Pattern: fmt: refusing to rewrite files with errors

From:    idef0.pl
Means:   A Markdown model's ```idef0 block is not closed; a ## doc
         comment is not followed by a line; svg was given a node that does
         not exist (idef0.pl dump lists them); fmt will not touch a file
         that does not lint.
Fix:     Close the fence with ```; fix the lint errors first, then fmt.

idef0: idef0_models in sysml.conf is auto, steps or root / ROOT has no steps agile-err-idef0-models

Pattern: idef0: idef0_models in sysml.conf is auto, steps or root, not '*' Pattern: idef0: * has no steps (action or calc usages) to draw; give it some, or set verb_root in sysml.conf

From:    model.pl idef0, model.pl docs
Means:   IDEF0 plates are drawn from the verb tree: the action (or calc) def
         named by verb_root and its steps. idef0_models chooses how: steps
         (one IDEF0 model per step, as Halberd), root (one model whose boxes
         are the steps, for steps without sub-steps, as Tidewater), or auto
         (root when every step is a leaf). The key has another value, or the
         verb root has no step usages.
Fix:     In sysml.conf write idef0_models = auto (or steps or root). Point
         verb_root at the action def at the top of the function tree
         (model.pl verbs shows it); it needs at least one step (action name
         : Def;) to draw.

idef0: skipped: sysml.conf sets no verb_root agile-err-idef0-skipped

Pattern: idef0: skipped: sysml.conf sets no verb_root (set it to the top action def to get docs/idef0/)

From:    model.pl docs
Means:   Not an error: docs wrote the other documents and exited 0. A new
         model has no function tree yet, so sysml.conf sets no verb_root
         and the IDEF0 plates (docs/idef0/) are left out. A fresh
         kickoff.pl scaffold starts this way, so its pipeline is green.
Fix:     Once the model has an action def at the top of its function tree,
         set verb_root = ThatDef in sysml.conf (model.pl verbs shows the
         candidates), run model.pl docs and commit docs/.

8. THE MODEL PORT AND SYSML TOOLS agile-errors-sysml

usage: xmi2sysml.pl ... / nothing to do / --req-style is def or usage agile-err-port-usage

Pattern: usage: xmi2sysml.pl Pattern: usage: reqif2sysml.pl Pattern: --req-style is def or usage Pattern: nothing to do: give --out DIR Pattern: xmi2sysml: * Pattern: reqif2sysml: *

From:    xmi2sysml.pl, reqif2sysml.pl
Means:   The command line is incomplete (no input file, or no --out,
         --stdout or --report), an option has a wrong value, or the input
         could not be read: the rest of the message names the file and the
         problem (exit 2). A message of the form FILE:LINE: ... after the
         tool name is an XML problem: see agile-err-xml.
Fix:     Give one input file and one of --out DIR, --stdout or --report
         (perl agile.pl help xmi2sysml / reqif2sysml). --req-style takes
         usage (the default) or def.

tools/sysml/sysml.pl not found; structural self-check only agile-err-port-no-checker

Pattern: tools/sysml/sysml.pl not found; structural self-check only

From:    xmi2sysml.pl --check, reqif2sysml.pl --check
Means:   --check runs the SysML v2 grammar checker over the output, and this
         copy of the kit has no tools/sysml. Only the tool's own structural
         check ran. A warning.
Fix:     Use a full copy of the kit (tools/sysml/ is part of it), or check
         the files later with perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl check.

FILE:LINE: end tag </X> does not match <Y> (and other XML errors) agile-err-xml

Pattern: unterminated comment Pattern: unterminated CDATA section Pattern: unterminated processing instruction Pattern: unterminated DOCTYPE Pattern: unterminated end tag Pattern: end tag </*> does not match <*> Pattern: end tag </*> with nothing open Pattern: unterminated start tag Pattern: empty tag Pattern: malformed attributes in <*> Pattern: missing end tag for <*> Pattern: no root element Pattern: parse_string: *

From:    XmlLite.pm, through xmi2sysml.pl, reqif2sysml.pl and status-
         metrics.pl init
Means:   The XMI or ReqIF file is not well-formed XML: it was cut off (a
         partial download or copy), edited by hand, or is not XML at all (a
         .mdzip, a zipped file renamed). The message names the line.
Fix:     Export again from Cameo or DOORS and copy the whole file. Open it
         at the line (vim +LINE FILE) to see the damage. Give xmi2sysml the
         model file (the one with <uml:Model>), not a profile file.

FILE: IO::Uncompress::Unzip is not available / not a zip / no .reqif file inside agile-err-reqifz

Pattern: IO::Uncompress::Unzip is not available in this Perl Pattern: not a zip (*) Pattern: no .reqif file inside the archive

From:    reqif2sysml.pl, Reqif.pm (a .reqifz)
Means:   A .reqifz is a zip holding the .reqif. This Perl cannot unzip, the
         file is not a zip, or no .reqif is inside it.
Fix:     Unzip it (unzip FILE.reqifz in Git Bash) and give the .reqif
         inside; or export plain ReqIF from DOORS.

FILE: no id column (have: ...); name it with --col id=NAME agile-err-doors-csv

Pattern: no rows Pattern: no column '*' (have: *) Pattern: no id column (have: *); name it with --col id=NAME Pattern: no text column (have: *); name it with --col text=NAME

From:    reqif2sysml.pl --csv
Means:   The DOORS CSV is empty, or its header has no column the tool
         recognises as the id or the text (Object Identifier, Object Text),
         or a --col names a column that is not there. The message lists the
         columns it has.
Fix:     Name the columns: --col id="ID" --col text="Requirement" (also
         heading, level, vm), spelled exactly as in the header. Check the
         separator with --sep ';' if the columns run together.

usage: status-metrics.pl {init,collect,report} ... error: ... agile-err-status-metrics-usage

Pattern: usage: status-metrics.pl {init,collect,report} Pattern: status-metrics.pl: error: *

From:    status-metrics.pl
Means:   The command or an option is wrong or missing: init needs --config
         --xmi --reqif; collect needs --config (and --history); report needs
         --config and --history (and --out). The error part says which.
Fix:     perl bin/status-metrics.pl COMMAND --help prints the options; the
         runbook is agile-howto-metrics-weekly.

json: expected ':' at offset N (metrics.json or history.jsonl) agile-err-status-metrics-json

Pattern: json: trailing data at offset * Pattern: json: expected ':' at offset * Pattern: json: expected ',' or '}' at offset * Pattern: json: expected ',' or ']' at offset * Pattern: json: unexpected input at offset * Pattern: json: unterminated string

From:    status-metrics.pl (reading metrics.json or a line of history.jsonl)
Means:   The JSON is malformed at that character offset: a missing comma or
         quote, a trailing comma, a comment (JSON has none), or a history
         line cut short by an interrupted collect.
Fix:     Open the file and go to the offset (in Vim: :goto N+1). For
         history.jsonl, delete a broken last line and collect that day again
         with --as-of DATE.

git ...: exit N / gen_cmd ...: exit N / tag ...: not baseline-<number> agile-err-status-metrics-git

Pattern: git *: exit * Pattern: gen_cmd *: exit * Pattern: git archive *: * Pattern: tag *: not baseline-<number> Pattern: git log *: not a two-parent merge Pattern: fork: * Pattern: chdir *: * Pattern: exec *: *

From:    status-metrics.pl collect
Means:   A command the collector runs failed: git (the repo path in
         metrics.json is wrong, or git is not on PATH), the gen_cmd or
         lint_cmd from metrics.json, or a repo convention is broken (a tag
         named baseline-something that is not baseline-N; a commit taken for
         a merge that has one parent).
Fix:     Run the same command by hand in the repo to see its error. Check
         repo, gen_cmd and lint_cmd in metrics.json. Rename a stray tag (git
         tag -d) so only baseline-N tags remain.

bad date / bad timestamp / FILE: no date agile-err-status-metrics-data

Pattern: bad timestamp: * Pattern: bad date: * Pattern: *: no date

From:    status-metrics.pl collect (the exports)
Means:   An export file has a date the collector cannot read (dates are
         YYYY-MM-DD, timestamps ISO 8601), or a runs/*/provenance.txt has no
         date= line.
Fix:     Fix the named file in the exports directory; the formats are in
         Appendix A of docs/STATUS-METRICS.html.

usage: perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl check FILE... / model.pl: no model/ directory agile-err-sysml-usage

Pattern: usage: perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl check FILE... Pattern: model.pl: no model/ directory Pattern: [--root DIR] COMMAND [options] Pattern: usage: * rename OLD NEW [--write] [--any] Pattern: usage: * libnames PATH/TO/sysml.library Pattern: cannot cd to *: * Pattern: timeout

From:    tools/sysml/sysml.pl, tools/sysml/model.pl
Means:   No command or a wrong one; or model.pl was run outside a project
         (it looks upward for a directory holding model/); or the Pilot
         engine stalled (validate, crosscheck: timeout).
Fix:     cd into the model project or give --root DIR (perl
         tools/sysml/model.pl --root examples/halberd lint). The command
         list prints with no arguments. A timeout only affects the optional
         Java checks.

new: NAME must be a PascalCase identifier / rename: 'X' already exists agile-err-model-new-rename

Pattern: new: NAME must be a PascalCase identifier Pattern: new: '*' already exists in Pattern: new: no Pattern: new: cannot find '*' in Pattern: rename: '*' is not a definition name Pattern: rename: '*' already exists Pattern: rename: '*' is a SysML keyword

From:    tools/sysml/model.pl new, rename
Means:   The new name is not PascalCase, is taken, or is a SysML keyword; or
         the --in PARENT is not a part def (new part) or a calc/action def
         (new verb); or the old name is not a definition.
Fix:     Pick another name (BeamControl, not beam_control); check the parent
         with model.pl nouns or verbs; rename --any renames any identifier;
         rename is a dry run until --write.

idef0: no calc def or action def named 'X' (verb_root in sysml.conf) agile-err-model-config

Pattern: idef0: no calc def or action def named '*' Pattern: backlog: cannot find the agile kit Pattern: install-hooks: * is not inside a git working tree

From:    tools/sysml/model.pl idef0, docs, backlog, install-hooks
Means:   sysml.conf's verb_root names no function in the model; backlog
         cannot find sim/idef0-backlog.pl; or the project is not in a git
         repository.
Fix:     Fix verb_root (and noun_root) in sysml.conf; give --agile=DIR or
         set AGILE_HOME to the kit; git init the model repository first.

usage: perl sysml-tree-svg.pl ... / sysml-check: X: no such file or directory agile-err-views-usage

Pattern: usage: perl sysml-tree-svg.pl Pattern: usage: perl sysml-trace-svg.pl Pattern: usage: perl sysml-ibd-svg.pl Pattern: usage: perl sysml-pkg-svg.pl Pattern: usage: perl sysml-plates.pl Pattern: usage: perl sysml-diff.pl Pattern: usage: perl sysml-threats.pl Pattern: usage: perl sysml-check.pl Pattern: usage: * draw tree|trace|ibd|pkg [-o FILE] [tool options] Pattern: sysml-*: *: no such file or directory Pattern: sysml-*: --changed needs --compare Pattern: sysml-plates: --size must be auto, A4, A3, A2, A1 or A0 Pattern: sysml-threats: --today must be YYYY-MM-DD Pattern: sysml-check: unknown check '*' (known: *) Pattern: sysml-check: *: * Pattern: sysml-*: no part def '*' Pattern: model.pl: * is missing (the tools/sysml/views toolkit) Pattern: usage: perl svg2tk.pl FILE.svg Pattern: svg2tk: cannot read *: * Pattern: svg2tk: *: no <svg> element Pattern: *.svg: * Pattern: */plates.html: *

From:    tools/sysml/views/*.pl, model.pl draw, plates, diff, threats,
         gate; svg2tk.pl (through bin/sysml-view.tcl)
Means:   A wrong option or value, no model directory or file, a --root
         that names no part def, --changed without --compare, or the
         output file or directory cannot be written. svg2tk: the drawer
         wrote no SVG (its own message is in the viewer's status line). "is missing": the
         kit copy has no tools/sysml/views (exit 2 in every case).
Fix:     model.pl draw takes tree, trace, ibd or pkg; run model.pl inside
         a project or with --root DIR before the command (a --root after
         it is the tool's: a part def name). model.pl nouns lists the part
         defs; --today and --date take YYYY-MM-DD. Get a fresh copy of the
         kit if the toolkit is missing (agile-sysml-views).

FILE:LINE: error: root package 'P' has no @Marking (and the other findings) agile-err-views-findings

Pattern: root package '*' has no @Marking Pattern: package '*' imports * package '*' Pattern: package '*' references * element '*' Pattern: text in * package '*' names * element '*' Pattern: package dependency cycle: * Pattern: crosses * with no satisfied security requirement Pattern: declares fromZone/toZone * but its ends sit in * Pattern: attack surface: * Pattern: connection end '*' is not a part or port of '*' Pattern: requirement * not satisfied Pattern: requirement * not verified Pattern: target '*' not found Pattern: target '*' is ambiguous; using the first Pattern: specializes unknown '*' Pattern: part '*' has type '*' that is not a part def here Pattern: recursive composition: '*' : * Pattern: view '*': expose '*' matches nothing Pattern: view '*': nothing to draw Pattern: view '*': render * is not supported Pattern: plate '*' could not be drawn Pattern: plate *: diagram text is * mm on *, below * mm

From:    model.pl gate, draw and plates; sysml-check.pl, sysml-pkg-svg.pl,
         sysml-ibd-svg.pl, sysml-trace-svg.pl, sysml-tree-svg.pl,
         sysml-plates.pl
Means:   A gate finding (agile-model-gate). Markings: every root package
         needs @Marking { level = Level::X; }; a lower package may not
         import or reference a higher one (write-down); a higher
         element's name in a lower package's text is a leak; packages
         should not depend on each other in a cycle. Zones: a connection
         between two trust zones needs a satisfied @SecurityRequirement,
         by its subject or named in the connection's secReq attribute;
         its fromZone/toZone attributes must say what @TrustZone says.
         Trace: a leaf requirement is satisfied and verified, by itself
         or a group above it. A note is information, not a failure.
         Drawing warnings: a type or supertype the files given do not
         define (pass the whole model), a part that contains itself, a
         view whose expose or render the plates cannot draw, a plate
         whose text would print smaller than --min-text.
Fix:     Add the marking (and private import SecMeta::*;), mark the
         importing package at least as high or move the element, rename
         the leaking text; add or name the covering requirement and its
         satisfy; fix the zone attributes or the @TrustZone; add the
         satisfy or verify. model.pl draw pkg / ibd / trace shows each
         finding in red; perl agile.pl help agile-sysml-views.

threat 'T' is not mitigated by any requirement / no CAPEC id agile-err-views-threats

Pattern: threat '*' is not mitigated by any requirement Pattern: threat '*' is mitigated only by requirements that are not * Pattern: threat '*': no STRIDE category Pattern: threat '*': STRIDE category '*' is not one of the six Pattern: threat '*': no CAPEC id Pattern: threat '*': CAPEC id '*' is not CAPEC-n Pattern: threat '*': mitigation = "*" but no @Mitigates on '*' names it Pattern: threat '*': @Mitigates on * but mitigation = "" Pattern: @Mitigates on requirement '*' names unknown threat '*' Pattern: @Mitigates on requirement '*' names no threat Pattern: risk acceptance on threat '*' * Pattern: accepted by risk acceptance

From:    model.pl threats and gate; sysml-threats.pl
Means:   Every threat needs one of the six STRIDE categories (Spoofing,
         Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of
         service, Elevation of privilege) and a CAPEC-n id, and a
         @Mitigates { threat = "T"; } on a requirement that is satisfied
         and verified. The status-metrics line form also carries
         mitigation = "REQ": it must name the same requirement. A risk
         acceptance needs an approver and an expiry date not yet past;
         a current one makes the open threat a listed warning.
Fix:     Add the mitigating requirement (with @Mitigates, a satisfy and a
         verify), or a @RiskAcceptance with approver and expires; correct
         the category or the id; keep mitigation and @Mitigates in step.
         --today YYYY-MM-DD pins the date for repeatable runs.

sysml-diff: 'git ls-tree ...' failed / REV: no .sysml files under PATH agile-err-views-diff

Pattern: sysml-diff: 'git *' failed Pattern: sysml-diff: 'git show *' failed Pattern: sysml-diff: *: no .sysml files under * Pattern: sysml-diff: * failed Pattern: *-changes.txt: *

From:    model.pl diff, sysml-diff.pl
Means:   git does not know the revision, the current directory is not
         in the repository, or the revision has no .sysml files under the
         paths; or one of the view tools the diff runs failed (its message
         is above).
Fix:     Run inside the model's git repository (Git Bash); git tag and git
         log --oneline show what OLD..NEW can be; give the path to the
         model (model.pl diff adds model/ when no path is given).

v1v2: FILE: no XMI or ReqIF member found / doors2v2: FILE: empty file agile-err-v1v2-doors2v2

Pattern: v1v2: * Pattern: doors2v2: * Pattern: usage: perl doors2v2.pl Pattern: *: error: no closing '*' Pattern: *: error: unexpected </*> Pattern: *: error: unclosed <*> Pattern: *: error: malformed XML*

From:    tools/sysml/v1v2.pl, tools/sysml/doors2v2.pl (agile-v1v2)
Means:   The command line is incomplete or an option has a bad value (an
         identifier is expected for --package and --marking), or an input
         cannot be read: a .mdzip without a model member, a zip the core
         unzip cannot open, a CSV with broken quoting, a --typemap line
         that is not KEY<TAB>V2TYPE[<TAB>UNIT]. FILE:LINE: error: ... is
         an XML problem at that line. "using member" says which file of a
         .mdzip was read (information, exit 0).
Fix:     perl tools/sysml/v1v2.pl with no arguments prints its usage.
         Unzip a .mdzip or .reqifz by hand if the zip module is missing
         and pass the member; re-export a broken XML or CSV file from
         Cameo or DOORS. The main path for exports it can read is
         xmi2sysml.pl / reqif2sysml.pl (agile-err-port-usage).

--layout-map FILE:LINE: expected PACKAGE = folder/ or PACKAGE = folder/File.sysml agile-err-layout-map

Pattern: *:*: expected PACKAGE = folder/ or PACKAGE = folder/File.sysml Pattern: *:*: no package name before '=' Pattern: *:*: no path after '=' for * Pattern: *:*: *: give a path relative to the output folder, without '..' Pattern: *:*: *: a file must end in .sysml (or end the folder with /) Pattern: *:*: '*' must be a folder (end it with /) Pattern: *:*: * is mapped twice

From:    xmi2sysml.pl --layout-map FILE, reqif2sysml.pl --layout-map FILE
Means:   The layout map puts each top-level package (or DOORS module) at a
         fixed path, so every drop lands in the same files and vendor merges
         stay three-way. A line in it is malformed: no =, no name or path, a
         path outside the output folder, a file not ending in .sysml, a *
         default that is not a folder, or a package listed twice.
Fix:     One line per package: Stations = physical/stations/ (a folder,
         ending in /) or Types = library/Types.sysml (a file). # starts a
         comment; * = unsorted/ sets the default. Keep one map for the
         project (examples/tidewater-v1/layout.map is a worked one) and use
         it for every drop.

FILE: not an xmi2sysml map / not a CHANGES.csv / --impact DIR: not a directory agile-err-xmi-map

Pattern: *: not an xmi2sysml map (expected the header xmi_id,v1_type,v1_qualified_name,v2_qualified_name,v2_kind,file,line) Pattern: *: not a CHANGES.csv (expected the header cr_id,title,rationale,kind,xmi_ids,requirements) Pattern: *: not a directory

From:    xmi2sysml.pl --delta OLD NEW --impact DIR [--map FILE]
Means:   The impact report reads the government's v2 model folder
         (--impact), optionally the old drop's v1-to-v2 map (--map, written
         by an earlier conversion), and the prime's change-request list
         (CHANGES.csv beside NEW.xmi). The folder is not a folder, the map
         was not written by xmi2sysml, or the CHANGES.csv beside the new
         drop is some other file.
Fix:     --impact takes the model folder, usually model/. Regenerate the map
         with xmi2sysml.pl --out DIR --map FILE OLD.xmi, or leave --map off
         (the old drop is converted on the fly). Fix or remove a stray
         CHANGES.csv; the prime's has the header
         cr_id,title,rationale,kind,xmi_ids,requirements.

req-recipe: --format is text, csv, junit or codequality / cannot read FILE agile-err-req-recipe

Pattern: usage: req-recipe.pl * Pattern: req-recipe: --format is text, csv, junit or codequality, not '*' Pattern: req-recipe: --require takes 'classification', not '*' Pattern: req-recipe: *

From:    tools/sysml/req-recipe.pl (the pipeline's recipe job)
Means:   The requirement recipe checker grades requirement text from .sysml
         files, DOORS ReqIF or CSV, or plain text. An option has a value it
         does not know, or an input or output path is wrong (the message
         names it).
Fix:     --format text|csv|junit|codequality; --require classification is
         the only part that can be made required. Check the input path and
         that a DOORS file is an export (agile-howto-doors). Findings are
         not errors: --strict makes them fail.

9. CODING DRILLS agile-errors-drills

Messages from drills/drill.pl and the test runner (agile-drills). drill.pl prints the usage line for a missing argument; perl drills/drill.pl help COMMAND has the details.

drill: no problem matches 'X' agile-err-drill-no-problem

Pattern: drill: no problem matches '*' Pattern: drill: '*' matches several problems: * Pattern: drill: no section '*'

From:    drill.pl show, start, test, check, solution, log, list
Means:   The id is not one of the problems under drills/, or a shortened
         id fits more than one (p2 is every t2 rung), or the section name
         is wrong.
Fix:     perl drills/drill.pl list shows every id and section; type
         enough of the id to be unique (p23, two-sum), or the whole id
         from the list.

drill: no file FILE (perl drills/drill.pl start ID first) agile-err-drill-no-file

Pattern: drill: no file * (perl drills/drill.pl start * first) Pattern: drill: no file * (perl drills/drill.pl phased 1 first)

From:    drill.pl test, phased test
Means:   There is no solution file of yours to test: the problem was not
         started in this workspace, or the workspace is another one (the
         default is ~/drills-work; --dir and $DRILLS_WORK change it).
Fix:     perl drills/drill.pl start ID (or phased 1), or pass the file:
         drill.pl test ID path/to/file.pl. Same --dir on every command.

drill: no attempt recorded for ID yet agile-err-drill-no-attempt

Pattern: drill: no attempt recorded for * yet: *

From:    drill.pl solution, phased solution
Means:   The reference is shown only after an attempt: a start or a test
         of that problem in this workspace. That keeps the binder's rule,
         read a solution only after a timed attempt.
Fix:     Start it and try (drill.pl start ID, drill.pl test ID). If you
         really need it now: drill.pl solution ID --force (the look is
         logged).

drill: usage: drill.pl COMMAND ... agile-err-drill-usage

Pattern: drill: usage: * Pattern: drill: unknown command '*' (perl drills/drill.pl help) Pattern: drill: '*' is not a number of minutes * Pattern: drill: *

From:    drill.pl
Means:   A command without its argument, a misspelt command, or a log
         line whose minutes are not a whole number. A message starting
         "drill:" that is not listed here comes from the same tool: it
         names the problem.
Fix:     perl drills/drill.pl help (the commands), drill.pl help COMMAND;
         minutes are whole numbers: drill.pl log p12 14 pass "note".

drill: phased: no scenario 'X' / no phase N agile-err-drill-phased

Pattern: drill: phased: no scenario '*' (there are: *) Pattern: drill: phased: no scenarios under drills/phased/ Pattern: drill: phased: no phase *

From:    drill.pl phased
Means:   The phase is not 1 to 4, the scenario name is not one under
         drills/phased/ (sensors, payments), or that folder is missing
         from this copy of the kit.
Fix:     perl drills/drill.pl phased lists the plan and the scenarios;
         phased 1, phased test 1, ... phased 4; --scenario payments.

your file does not load / timeout after 5s / exit(N) called agile-err-drill-tests

Pattern: drill: cannot load tests *: * Pattern: your file does not load: * Pattern: timeout after *s Pattern: not run: an earlier case timed out Pattern: exit(*) called: return a value instead

From:    drill.pl test and check (the test runner in lib/Drills.pm)
Means:   Your file has a syntax error or dies while loading (the line
         number is in the message); a case ran past its time limit (an
         endless loop: the rest of the cases are skipped); your function
         called exit, which would end the whole run. "cannot load tests"
         means the kit's own tests.pl is broken.
Fix:     perl -c ~/drills-work/ID.pl shows the syntax error. Return the
         answer from the function instead of printing it or calling
         exit; stdin problems print and end normally. Check every loop
         moves toward its end (lo/hi, a queue that empties). A broken
         tests.pl: get a fresh copy of the kit.

10. GITLAB, GITFLOW AND THE PIPELINE agile-errors-gitlab

gitlab.pl, the GitLab and GitFlow libraries behind it, the pipeline's ci/job.pl and the team tools kickoff.pl, talk.pl and ci-reports.pl. Messages that start "GitLab:" come from the server (or the offline emulator) and end with the HTTP status GitLab itself would answer, so the same fix works on both.

gitlab.pl: unknown command / --OPTION needs a value / mr new needs --source and --title agile-err-gitlab-usage

Pattern: gitlab.pl: --* needs a value Pattern: gitlab.pl: unknown option * Pattern: gitlab.pl: unknown command '*' (gitlab.pl help) Pattern: gitlab.pl: sprint COUNT must be a number Pattern: gitlab.pl: issue note needs TEXT or --file FILE Pattern: gitlab.pl: mr new needs --source BRANCH and --title TITLE Pattern: gitlab.pl: --var is KEY=VALUE Pattern: gitlab.pl: schedule new needs --cron "MIN HOUR DOM MON DOW" and --ref BRANCH Pattern: gitlab.pl: schedule next needs a CRON line Pattern: gitlab.pl: no wiki page '*' Pattern: gitlab.pl: *

From:    gitlab.pl (every command)
Means:   The command line is incomplete or misspelled: an option without its
         value, an unknown option or command, a missing argument the command
         needs, or a wiki page that does not exist.
Fix:     gitlab.pl help lists the commands; gitlab.pl help COMMAND shows one
         command's arguments (agile-gitlab). Quote values with spaces:
         --title "Close the Stations TODOs".

gitlab.pl: give --url URL or --local DIR / set VAR to a personal or project access token agile-err-gitlab-connect

Pattern: gitlab.pl: give --url URL (or GITLAB_URL) or --local DIR (the emulator) Pattern: gitlab.pl: give --project GROUP/NAME (or GITLAB_PROJECT) Pattern: GitLab: give url => URL (a GitLab server) or local => DIR (the emulator) Pattern: GitLab: set * to a personal or project access token (scope api) Pattern: talk: give --local DIR (the emulator) or --url URL (or GITLAB_LOCAL / GITLAB_URL) Pattern: talk: give --project GROUP/NAME (or GITLAB_PROJECT) Pattern: kickoff: no --local DIR or --url URL (or GITLAB_URL): which GitLab?

From:    gitlab.pl, talk.pl, kickoff.pl start
Means:   The tools do not know which GitLab to talk to (a server with --url,
         or the offline emulator in a folder with --local), which project,
         or the server's token is not in the environment variable named by
         --token-env (GITLAB_TOKEN by default).
Fix:     Set them once per shell: export
         GITLAB_URL=https://gitlab.example.gov
         GITLAB_PROJECT=tidewater/model GITLAB_TOKEN=... (a personal or
         project access token with scope api; never commit it). For
         practice: export GITLAB_LOCAL=DIR (a practice sandbox's env.sh does
         it).

GitLab: METHOD PATH: STATUS MESSAGE / curl exit N agile-err-gitlab-http

Pattern: GitLab: curl exit *: * Pattern: GitLab: * *: no HTTP status in curl's output Pattern: GitLab: * *: * * Pattern: GitLab: no artifact * from job * on * in * (curl exit *: *) Pattern: GitLab: package upload failed: * Pattern: GitLab: package download failed: *

From:    gitlab.pl, talk.pl and the libraries, against a GitLab server
Means:   The server answered with an error (the status and GitLab's own
         message are in the line: 401 a bad or expired token, 403 not
         allowed for your role, 404 a wrong project path or one you cannot
         see, 409 already exists, 422 a value GitLab rejected), or curl
         could not reach it (a network, proxy or certificate problem), or
         something between answered instead of GitLab.
Fix:     Read GitLab's message in the line first. 401: make a new token
         (Profile > Access tokens, scope api) and export it. 403: ask a
         maintainer for the role. 404: check --project (group/name, as in
         the project's URL). curl exit 6 or 7: the server name or the
         network/VPN; 60: the certificate (your organization's CA bundle,
         CURL_CA_BUNDLE). Try the same with --dry-run to see the request.

GitLab: FILE does not match the registry's sha256 agile-err-gitlab-sha

Pattern: GitLab: * does not match the registry's sha256

From:    gitlab.pl package get, the pipeline's intake job
Means:   The file downloaded from the package registry is not the file that
         was uploaded: its checksum differs from the one recorded at upload
         (a broken transfer, or someone replaced the package).
Fix:     Download it again. If it still differs, stop: do not import the
         drop; tell the security owner and the prime (the transmittal record
         has the checksums the prime sent).

GitLab: pipeline must succeed / approvals required / merge conflict agile-err-gitlab-merge

Pattern: GitLab: pipeline must succeed (pipeline #* *) (405 Method Not Allowed) Pattern: GitLab: pipeline must succeed (!* has no pipeline) (405 Method Not Allowed) Pattern: GitLab: approvals required: * needs *, has * (405 Method Not Allowed) Pattern: GitLab: code owner approval required for * (*) (405 Method Not Allowed) Pattern: GitLab: discussions not resolved (* open) (405 Method Not Allowed) Pattern: GitLab: merge conflict: !* cannot be merged into '*'; merge '*' into '*' and resolve (406 Branch cannot be merged) Pattern: GitLab: MR is not open (!* is *) (405 Method Not Allowed) Pattern: GitLab: MR !* is a draft; mark it ready first (405 Method Not Allowed) Pattern: GitLab: * is not allowed to merge into '*' (405 Method Not Allowed) Pattern: GitLab: merge request !* is not open Pattern: GitLab: source branch '*' no longer exists Pattern: GitLab: squash is not supported by the local emulator (the project merges with merge commits)

From:    gitlab.pl mr merge, gitlab.pl flow released
Means:   GitLab refused the merge because one of the project's rules is not
         met yet. These are the gates working: the pipeline is red or has
         not run, a code owner (CODEOWNERS) or the approval rule has not
         approved, a review thread is still open, the branch conflicts with
         its target, the merge request is a draft or closed, or your role
         may not merge into that branch.
Fix:     gitlab.pl mr show IID names what is missing. Red pipeline: read the
         failed job's log (gitlab.pl pipeline show ID), fix on the branch,
         push. Approvals: ask the code owner named in the message. Open
         threads: answer and resolve them. Conflict: on your branch, git
         merge origin/develop, fix the conflict markers in Vim, commit, push
         (agile-gitlab). Draft: /ready in a comment.

GitLab: USER wrote merge request !N and cannot approve it agile-err-gitlab-approve

Pattern: GitLab: * wrote merge request !* and cannot approve it (401 Unauthorized) Pattern: GitLab: * already approved merge request !* (401 Unauthorized) Pattern: GitLab: * has no access to approve in * (401 Unauthorized)

From:    gitlab.pl mr approve
Means:   An approval must come from someone other than the author, once,
         with at least the reporter role in the project. The review is the
         second pair of eyes a configuration change needs.
Fix:     Ask a teammate who is a code owner for the changed files
         (CODEOWNERS) to approve. In the emulator, act as them with --as
         USER.

You are not allowed to push code to protected branches on this project. agile-err-gitlab-protected

Pattern: You are not allowed to push code to protected branches on this project. Pattern: You are not allowed to force push code to a protected branch on this project. Pattern: You are not allowed to delete protected branches from this project. Pattern: You are not allowed to create this tag as it is protected. Pattern: You are not allowed to change existing tags on this project. Pattern: You are not allowed to push code to this project. Pattern: GitLab: you are not allowed to create this tag as it is protected (403 Forbidden) Pattern: GitLab: you are not allowed to push code to this project (403 Forbidden) Pattern: GitLab: you are not allowed to create branch '*' (403 Forbidden) Pattern: GitLab: * cannot publish packages to * (403 Forbidden) Pattern: GitLab: the deploy token cannot publish packages to * (403 Forbidden) Pattern: GitLab: * cannot create deploy tokens in * (403 Forbidden) Pattern: GitLab: * cannot create trigger tokens in * (403 Forbidden) Pattern: GitLab: invalid trigger token for * (404 Not Found)

From:    git push (the server's protection rules), gitlab.pl tag, package,
         token, trigger
Means:   main and develop are protected: changes reach them only through
         merge requests; baseline tags are protected: only maintainers
         create them and nobody moves or deletes them. Tokens and packages
         need the right role or scope. This is configuration control
         working, not a fault.
Fix:     Push your work to a feature branch and open a merge request
         (gitlab.pl flow start feature NAME ... flow finish). If you
         committed on develop by mistake, the primer's Rescue appendix shows
         how to move the commits to a branch. Tags and tokens: ask a
         maintainer. A deploy token needs the write_package_registry scope;
         a trigger token is shown once when made.

GitLab: no project 'PATH' / no branch or tag 'REF' / no milestone 'NAME' agile-err-gitlab-notfound

Pattern: GitLab: no project '*' (404 Project Not Found) Pattern: GitLab: no branch or commit '*' in * (400 Invalid reference name) Pattern: GitLab: no branch or commit '*' in * (400 Target * is invalid) Pattern: GitLab: no branch or tag '*' in * (400 Ref is invalid) Pattern: GitLab: source branch '*' does not exist in * Pattern: GitLab: target branch '*' does not exist in * Pattern: GitLab: tag '*' does not exist in * Pattern: GitLab: no milestone '*' in * Pattern: GitLab: no pipeline * in * Pattern: GitLab: no user '*' Pattern: GitLab: no file * to upload

From:    gitlab.pl (most commands)
Means:   The name does not exist on that GitLab: a misspelled project path,
         a branch that was not pushed (or already deleted after its merge),
         a sprint milestone not created, a user not added, or a local file
         path that is wrong.
Fix:     Check the spelling against GitLab (gitlab.pl mr list, issue list,
         git branch -r). Push the branch first (gitlab.pl flow publish).
         Sprint milestones: gitlab.pl sprints START COUNT, or setup with the
         project file.

GitLab: tag 'NAME' already exists / another open merge request already exists agile-err-gitlab-exists

Pattern: GitLab: project '*' already exists (400 has already been taken) Pattern: GitLab: milestone '*' already exists in * Pattern: GitLab: branch '*' already exists in * (400 Branch already exists) Pattern: GitLab: tag '*' already exists in * (400 Tag * already exists) Pattern: GitLab: release '*' already exists in * Pattern: GitLab: another open merge request already exists for this source branch: !*

From:    gitlab.pl
Means:   The thing you asked to create is already there. Tags and releases
         are never reused: a baseline name names one configuration forever.
Fix:     Use the existing one (the message names it), or choose a new name
         (baseline-2, not baseline-1 again). For a branch with an open merge
         request: push to it; the merge request updates by itself.

GitLab: bad time 'X' / unknown access level / an issue needs a title agile-err-gitlab-values

Pattern: GitLab: bad time '*' (want YYYY-MM-DD[THH:MM[:SS]]) Pattern: GitLab: unknown access level '*' (none, developer, maintainer, owner) Pattern: GitLab: issue_type is issue, task or incident, not '*' Pattern: GitLab: link type is relates_to, blocks or is_blocked_by, not '*' Pattern: GitLab: state_event is close or reopen, not '*' Pattern: GitLab: a package name is letters, digits and . _ - ('*') Pattern: GitLab: a package version is letters, digits and . _ + - ('*') Pattern: GitLab: a package file name is letters, digits and . _ + - ('*') Pattern: GitLab: an artifact path may not contain '..' ('*') Pattern: GitLab: deploy token scope is read_repository, read_registry, write_registry, read_package_registry or write_package_registry, not '*' Pattern: GitLab: analytics --by is sprint, week or month, not '*' Pattern: GitLab: project path '*' needs a group: group/name Pattern: GitLab: unknown time zone '*' (UTC, +HH:MM, America/New_York, America/Chicago, America/Denver, America/Los_Angeles, ...) Pattern: GitLab: an issue needs a title Pattern: GitLab: a merge request needs * Pattern: GitLab: a release needs tag_name Pattern: GitLab: a pipeline schedule needs *

From:    gitlab.pl and the project file
Means:   A value is not one GitLab accepts; the message lists the allowed
         ones.
Fix:     Use one of the listed values. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD (or
         YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM); projects are group/name; time zones are UTC,
         +HH:MM or a US zone name.

GitLab: bad cron 'LINE': want 5 fields / cron 'LINE' never runs agile-err-gitlab-cron

Pattern: GitLab: bad cron '*': want 5 fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) Pattern: GitLab: bad cron '*': '*' is not a * (*-*) Pattern: GitLab: bad cron '*': step '*' in the * field Pattern: GitLab: bad cron '*': range '*' runs backwards Pattern: GitLab: cron '*' never runs Pattern: GitLab: more than 10000 scheduled runs before *: check the cron lines Pattern: GitLab: run_due_schedules is for the local emulator; a GitLab server runs its schedules itself Pattern: GitLab: schedule * skipped: * does not exist yet; re-run setup after flow init

From:    gitlab.pl schedule, setup ([schedules] in the project file)
Means:   A pipeline schedule's cron line is malformed (five fields: minute
         hour day-of-month month day-of-week), can never fire (0 0 31 2 *),
         or fires so often that a long span would run thousands of
         pipelines. A schedule on a branch that does not exist yet (develop
         before flow init) is skipped with a warning.
Fix:     Preview a line with gitlab.pl schedule next "0 2 * * 1-5" --tz
         America/New_York -n 5. Fields: minute 0-59, hour 0-23, day 1-31,
         month 1-12 or jan-dec, weekday 0-7 or sun-sat. Run setup again
         after gitlab.pl flow init to create the skipped schedules.

FILE:LINE: label value is '#RRGGBB | description' (the project file) agile-err-gitlab-projectfile

Pattern: *: [project] needs path = group/name Pattern: *:*: a key before any [section] Pattern: *:*: expected KEY = VALUE Pattern: *:*: label value is '#RRGGBB | description' Pattern: *:*: branch rule words are push:LEVEL merge:LEVEL force:yes|no codeowners:yes|no Pattern: *:*: tag rule is create:LEVEL Pattern: *:*: approval rule is N user user ... Pattern: *:*: a schedule is CRON | REF [| TZ [| K=V ...]] Pattern: *:*: schedule variables are KEY=VALUE, not '*'

From:    gitlab.pl setup FILE, setup --diff FILE, kickoff.pl start
Means:   A line in the project file (project.conf) does not follow its
         format. The file is INI-like: [sections] of KEY = VALUE lines; each
         section has its own value form.
Fix:     Compare the line with tools/gitlab/templates/project.conf, which
         has a commented example of every section. Inline comments start
         with " ;" (space semicolon), because label colours use #.

GitFlow: origin has no 'develop' branch (run init first) / not a feature branch agile-err-gitflow

Pattern: GitFlow: start feature, release or hotfix, not '*' Pattern: GitFlow: a branch name is letters, digits and . _ - / ('*') Pattern: GitFlow: origin has no '*' branch (run init first) Pattern: GitFlow: branch '*' already exists on origin Pattern: GitFlow: '*' is not a feature, release or hotfix branch Pattern: GitFlow: merge request !* is not merged yet Pattern: GitFlow: !* did not go into * Pattern: GitFlow: take ours or theirs, not '*' Pattern: GitFlow: this step needs a GitLab connection (gl => GitLab->new(...)) Pattern: GitFlow: * already exists Pattern: gitlab.pl: flow pushes to the repository; --dry-run does not apply to it Pattern: gitlab.pl: flow runs inside a clone of the project (no git repository here)

From:    gitlab.pl flow init|start|publish|finish|released|take
Means:   The gitflow step does not fit where you are: flow runs in a clone
         of the model project; start needs feature, release or hotfix and a
         simple name; finish runs on such a branch; released runs after the
         release merge request is merged into main; develop must exist (flow
         init makes it). --dry-run cannot preview flow, because flow pushes
         with git.
Fix:     cd into your clone. git branch shows where you are. Start work with
         gitlab.pl flow start feature 12-short-name (from develop). Merge
         the release MR first, then gitlab.pl flow released IID. take is
         ours or theirs (agile-gitlab).

GitFlow: drop DIR changes nothing on vendor/prime / merging failed agile-err-gitflow-vendor

Pattern: GitFlow: vendor import needs drop => DIR (got *) Pattern: GitFlow: vendor import needs version => NAME (letters, digits, . _ -) Pattern: GitFlow: vendor import needs convert => sub { my (*, *) = *; ... } Pattern: GitFlow: origin/* has no root commit Pattern: GitFlow: drop * changes nothing on * Pattern: GitFlow: merging * into * failed: * Pattern: GitFlow: no .xmi file in *

From:    gitlab.pl flow vendor DROPDIR VERSION
Means:   The prime drop could not be imported onto the vendor branch: the
         drop folder has no .xmi file, the version name is missing or odd,
         the drop is identical to the last one imported, or git could not
         merge the vendor branch into the new feature branch (other than an
         ordinary conflict, which is reported as conflicted files).
Fix:     Point flow vendor at the unpacked drop folder (with tidewater.xmi,
         .reqif, MANIFEST.txt) and give the prime's version (v1.1). An
         identical drop needs no import: record it on the Prime Drop issue.
         For a failed merge, run git status in the clone and read git's
         message.

GitFlow: model.pl check gave no violation count agile-err-gitflow-allowance

Pattern: GitFlow: tools/sysml/model.pl check gave no violation count: *

From:    gitlab.pl flow vendor, gitlab.pl flow allowance VERSION
Means:   After a drop is merged, flow records the drop's outline count in
         .ci/outline-max. It runs the kit's model.pl check for that count,
         and the check printed no count: the kit is not where KIT says, or
         the model/ folder or sysml.conf cannot be read.
Fix:     Check that KIT points at the kit (perl $KIT/tools/sysml/model.pl
         check works in the clone), then run gitlab.pl flow allowance
         VERSION again.

FILE:LINE: job 'NAME': stage 'X' is not in stages / include: local file does not exist agile-err-gitlab-ci-yaml

Pattern: *: !reference nested too deeply (a cycle?) Pattern: *: * must be a map Pattern: *: extends: '*' is not defined Pattern: *: extends: circular chain through '*' Pattern: *: extends: more than 11 levels at '*' Pattern: *: include: an item must be a path or a map (local:, template:, project:, remote:, component:) Pattern: *: include: cycle * Pattern: *: include: local file '*' does not exist (paths start at the repository root) Pattern: *: include: local file '*' must end in .yml or .yaml Pattern: *: include: local: needs a path Pattern: *: include: more than * included files Pattern: *: include: rules must be a list of maps Pattern: *: include: rules: when must be always or never, got '*' Pattern: *: job '*' extends '*', which is not defined Pattern: *: job '*' has no script (or trigger) Pattern: *: job '*' must be a map of keys Pattern: *: job '*': a * line is a map (*) -- quote a command that contains ': ' Pattern: *: job '*': rules cannot be used with only/except Pattern: *: job '*': rules must be a list of maps Pattern: *: job '*': stage '*' is not in stages (*) Pattern: *: job '*': unknown when '*' Pattern: *: stages must be a list Pattern: *: workflow:rules must be a list of maps Pattern: *:*: !reference [*] not found Pattern: *:1: the top level must be a map of keys Pattern: rules:if: bad regular expression /*/ in '*' Pattern: rules:if: cannot read '*' at '*'

From:    gitlab.pl ci (the local pipeline runner, lib/GitLabCI.pm), the
         emulator's pipelines
Means:   The pipeline file (.gitlab-ci.yml or a file it includes) breaks
         GitLab's rules at that file and line. GitLab would reject the same
         file. The commonest: an unquoted script line containing ": " (YAML
         reads it as a map), a job naming a stage that stages: does not
         list, a misspelled extends: parent, an include path not starting at
         the repository root.
Fix:     Open the file at the line (in Vim: :e +LINE FILE). Quote a script
         line that contains ": " ('perl ci/job.pl lint' is safe; "echo a: b"
         must be quoted). gitlab.pl ci --list shows which jobs a pipeline
         would run, without running them. GitLab's own CI/CD > Editor also
         validates the file.

gitlab.pl ci: not inside a git work tree / --event tag needs --tag T agile-err-gitlab-ci-cli

Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: not inside a git work tree Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: no * here or at the top of the work tree (pass --file) Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: a merge request pipeline needs a branch (check one out or pass --branch) Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: HEAD is detached: pass --branch B Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: --event tag needs --tag T (HEAD has no tag) Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: --var needs KEY=VALUE, got '*' Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: unknown --event '*' (push, merge_request_event, tag, schedule, web, trigger) Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: unexpected argument '*' * Pattern: gitlab.pl ci: *

From:    gitlab.pl ci (run the pipeline locally)
Means:   The local run needs a clone with a pipeline file and enough context
         to pick jobs the way GitLab would: the branch (or tag) and the kind
         of pipeline.
Fix:     cd into the clone. gitlab.pl ci --list --event merge_request_event
         --target develop previews a merge request pipeline; --event push
         --branch develop a develop pipeline; --event tag --tag baseline-1 a
         baseline. --var KEY=VALUE sets a CI/CD variable.

KIT is not set / the kit on this runner is X, but .kit-version pins Y agile-err-ci-job

Pattern: usage: perl ci/job.pl * Pattern: KIT is not set: add it under Settings > CI/CD > Variables (the kit's path on the runner) Pattern: KIT=* does not hold the agile kit (no tools/sysml/model.pl) Pattern: the kit on this runner is *, but .kit-version pins *

From:    ci/job.pl (every pipeline job of the model project)
Means:   Every job calls the kit's tools through the CI/CD variable KIT, the
         kit's folder on the runner. It is not set, points at the wrong
         folder, or the runner has a different kit version than the one the
         model project pins in .kit-version (toolchain changes are reviewed
         like model changes).
Fix:     Settings > CI/CD > Variables: KIT = the kit's path on the runner
         (C:/agile on a Windows runner; /opt/agile-kit in the mbse-ci Docker
         image). To move to a new kit version, bump .kit-version in a merge
         request, or put the runner back on the pinned version.

kickoff: DIR is not empty / --levels is a comma list of names agile-err-kickoff

Pattern: usage: kickoff.pl * Pattern: kickoff: --project is GROUP/NAME, not '*' Pattern: kickoff: * is not empty (use an empty or new folder, or --force) Pattern: kickoff: no templates in * (is this the agile kit?) Pattern: kickoff: cannot enter *: * Pattern: kickoff: git init failed: * Pattern: kickoff: git add failed: * Pattern: kickoff: git commit failed: * Pattern: kickoff: --drop needs --version (e.g. v1.0) Pattern: kickoff: --levels is a comma list of names, top level first (e.g. L1Network,L2Segment,L3Station) Pattern: kickoff: scaffold needs a DIR Pattern: kickoff: no layout map *

From:    tools/gitlab/kickoff.pl doctor|scaffold|start
Means:   scaffold makes a new model repository from the kit's templates in
         an empty folder; start runs the week-zero steps. The folder is not
         empty, an argument is malformed (--layout-map names no file), the
         kit's templates are missing (kickoff.pl was copied out of the
         kit), or git failed (its message follows).
Fix:     Use a new folder: perl $KIT/tools/gitlab/kickoff.pl scaffold model
         --project tidewater/model --levels L1Network,L2Segment,L3Station.
         Run kickoff.pl from inside the kit. A git failure: run kickoff.pl
         doctor, which checks git's version and identity (git config
         user.name / user.email). start --from N resumes after a failed
         step. --layout-map takes the path of an existing map, e.g. the
         kit's examples/tidewater-v1/layout.map.

talk: standup needs --as USER / no milestone 'Sprint N' agile-err-talk

Pattern: usage: talk.pl * Pattern: talk: no journal at * Pattern: talk: standup needs --as USER Pattern: talk: review needs --sprint N Pattern: talk: --sprint is a number, not '*' Pattern: talk: --date is YYYY-MM-DD, not '*' Pattern: talk: no milestone 'Sprint *' Pattern: talk: milestone '*' has no start date Pattern: talk: milestone '*' has no due date Pattern: talk: translate needs FILE or - (standard input) Pattern: talk: unknown command '*' (standup, review, weekly, translate, help) Pattern: talk: unexpected argument '*'

From:    tools/gitlab/talk.pl standup|review|weekly|translate
Means:   talk.pl drafts words from GitLab and the journal; it needs to know
         whose stand-up (--as), which sprint (--sprint, matching a milestone
         named "Sprint N" with start and due dates), and where the journal
         is (--journal, a daily.pl project).
Fix:     talk.pl standup --as bob; talk.pl review --sprint 4; talk.pl
         translate notes.txt (or - to read what you paste). Sprint
         milestones need dates: gitlab.pl sprints START COUNT makes them.

ci-reports: no 'elements=N errors=E warnings=W' line in LOG agile-err-ci-reports

Pattern: usage: ci-reports.pl * Pattern: ci-reports: no 'elements=N errors=E warnings=W' line in * (is it model.pl lint output?) Pattern: ci-reports: no '* tag mismatches' or 'violations' line in * (is it model.pl check output?) Pattern: ci-reports: no 'C requirements linked' line in * (is it reqif2sysml.pl --report --model output?)

From:    tools/gitlab/ci-reports.pl (inside ci/job.pl's grammar, lint,
         outline, todo and trace jobs)
Means:   ci-reports turns a checker's output into GitLab's merge-request
         reports (JUnit, Code Quality, metrics). It was given the wrong log
         for its mode, or the checker failed before printing its summary
         line.
Fix:     Read the job log above this line: the checker's own error is there.
         Run ci/job.pl NAME rather than ci-reports by hand; it passes the
         right log to the right mode.

GitLab: no user given / cannot save STDOUT (a script or the kit itself) agile-err-gitlab-internal

Pattern: GitLab: add_note kind is issue or mr, not '*' Pattern: GitLab: a merge request pipeline needs mr_iid Pattern: GitLab: job_artifact needs * Pattern: GitLab: no user given Pattern: GitLab: cannot create * Pattern: GitLab: cannot store *: * Pattern: GitLab: git *: * Pattern: GitFlow: new needs * Pattern: GitFlow: git *: * Pattern: GitFlow: git clone *: * Pattern: GitFlow: copy */*: * Pattern: GitLab: * Pattern: cannot save STDOUT: * Pattern: cannot save STDERR: * Pattern: cannot redirect STDOUT: * Pattern: cannot redirect STDERR: * Pattern: cannot restore STDOUT: * Pattern: cannot restore STDERR: * Pattern: kickoff: cannot save STDOUT: * Pattern: kickoff: cannot save STDERR: * Pattern: kickoff: cannot redirect STDOUT: * Pattern: kickoff: cannot redirect STDERR: * Pattern: kickoff: cannot restore STDOUT: * Pattern: kickoff: cannot restore STDERR: *

From:    lib/GitLab.pm, lib/GitFlow.pm, lib/GitLabCI.pm used from a script,
         ci/job.pl, kickoff.pl
Means:   A script called the GitLab or GitFlow library without a required
         argument, or a file or git operation underneath failed (a full
         disk, a folder that is not writable, or git's own error, which
         follows the message). The STDOUT/STDERR lines mean the tool could
         not capture a job's output: almost always a full disk or a temp
         folder that is not writable.
Fix:     Read git's or the system's words at the end of the line. Check free
         space and that the temp folder (TMP/TMPDIR) and the emulator folder
         are writable. In your own scripts, pass every argument the method's
         header comment names. If the kit's own commands print it with
         nothing wrong on disk, report it with the command you ran.

11. INTERNAL INVARIANTS agile-err-internal

These messages mean a bug in the kit or a broken copy of it, not something you did. Note the command you ran and the message, and get a fresh copy of the kit (git status shows local changes; git checkout -- FILE restores one).

Internal: : unknown function '*' Internal: : empty list Internal: range: zero step Internal: chunksOf: n must be > 0 Internal: unwrap: *
